articles.title: El tenso cara a cara entre James y Teófilo Gutiérrez en el Nacional vs. Junior ¿Qué se dijeron?
articles.standfirst: El picante momento entre James Rodríguez y Teo Gutiérrez en pleno partido: ¡Se dijeron de todo!
articles.summary: El picante momento entre James Rodríguez y Teo Gutiérrez en pleno partido: ¡Se dijeron de todo!
articles.body: El duelo entre Atlético Nacional y Junior de Barranquilla en el Atanasio Girardot no solo ofreció emociones en el marcador con el triunfo verdolaga 3-1, sino también un duelo aparte cargado de tensión, provocaciones y viejas rencillas entre dos referentes históricos del fútbol colombiano: James Rodríguez y Teófilo Gutiérrez. Lo que en algún momento fue una sociedad dorada en la Selección Colombia que brilló en el Mundial de Brasil 2014, se transformó en un intenso choque de carácteres vistiendo las camisetas de dos de los rivales más grandes de la Liga BetPlay. La tensión comenzó a gestarse desde el primer tiempo. Tras una asistencia magistral de James para el gol de Andrés Felipe Román, el volante de Atlético Nacional cayó al césped tras un leve choque con Deiber Caicedo. La jugada fue interpretada por 'Teo' como una simulación, lo que provocó el reclamo inmediato del atacante 'Tiburón'. Gutiérrez se acercó a reprocharle airadamente la acción a James, marcando el terreno para lo que sería un cara a cara aún más picante en la segunda mitad. En la parte complementaria, los ánimos subieron de tono. Tras una disputa de balón, ambos futbolistas se buscaron en el terreno de juego, quedando frente a frente entre reclamos y ademanes. Teófilo le levantó la mano a James recriminándole alguna frase vertida en caliente, mientras el referente verdolaga le contestaba a poca distancia. Las imágenes televisivas captaron el momento exacto en el que ambos referentes intercambiaron palabras subidas de tono, dejando claro que dentro del campo la amistad con la camiseta tricolor quedó temporalmente en pausa. “Eso no se dice, eso no se dice. Eso es entre los dos”, le habría dicho el delantero juniorista a James. Las cámaras captan como Teo le insiste: “Cuidadito eh, cuidadito. Eso no se dice, con respeto”. Teo no acabó nada contento con la acción y por eso le reprochó a James: “Yo a ti te respeto, espero que tu también”. El choque en Medellín no fue casualidad. En los días previos al partido, ya existía un ambiente caldeado por declaraciones cruzadas y el trasfondo de la contratación de James por parte del cuadro paisa, un fichaje que había resonado fuertemente en el entorno de Junior. Finalmente, Atlético Nacional logró imponerse en el marcador, pero las miradas se las llevó el cara a cara entre dos figuras de un peso enorme en el FPC, demostrando que la jerarquía y el carácter competitivo de ambos sigue intacto.

articles.title: Indian men's squash team lose 1-2 to Malaysia, sign off with bronze medal at Asian Games
articles.summary: India's men's squash team signed off with bronze medal after losing their semifinal match against Malaysia at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Thursday.
articles.body: India's men's squash team signed off with bronze medal after losing their semifinal match against Malaysia at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Thursday.The men's team lost 1-2 to Malaysia, with Veer Chotrani's comeback win keeping India in the contest before Velavan Senthilkumar's defeat ended their hopes of reaching the final.Abhay Singh had opened the tie against Malaysia's Eain Yow, with India hoping to reach final to repeat their gold-medal performance from Hangzhou 2022. However, the 28-year-old lost 3-0 (11-8, 11-8, 11-8) in the opening match.Chotrani then kept India's hopes alive with a 3-0 (11-4, 11-8, 11-5) win over Sanjay Jeeva.With the semifinal tied at 1-1, Velavan faced Ameeshenraj Chandaran in the deciding match. Despite winning the first game, Velavan lost 3-1 (12-10, 11-6, 11-8, 11-9), handing Malaysia a place in the final.The result meant India could not defend the men's team gold they won at the 2022 Asian Games (played in 2023) in Hangzhou.Earlier in the day, the Indian women's team also lost 1-2 to Hong Kong in the semifinal and won bronze.India were hoping to better their Hangzhou 2022 performance, but Anahat Singh's opening-match defeat put them under pressure. The 18-year-old world No. 17 squandered four match points before losing 2-3 (11-9, 11-8, 6-11, 11-13, 10-12) to world No. 25 Sin Yuk Chan in a match that went to five games.World No. 73 Tanvi Khanna then brought India back into contention with a 1-3 (4-11, 13-11, 11-9, 13-11) win over world No. 40 Ka Yi Lee.However, veteran Joshna Chinappa could not complete the comeback. articles.title: ”Se ha equivocado en las formas, pero Cristiano Ronaldo no se merece ese adiós a Portugal”
articles.standfirst: 'El Corrillo' es el espacio de debate de Directo MARCA
articles.summary: 'El Corrillo' es el espacio de debate de Directo MARCA
articles.body: María José Hostalrich, Manu Martín, Joan Prats, José Luis Allegue, y Javi Estepa han sido los tertulianos de 'El Corrillo' en 'Directo MARCA' con Rafa Sahuquillo en Radio MARCA, en un debate que ha protagonizado el conflicto de Cristiano Ronaldo con la selección portuguesa. La salida de Cristiano Ronaldo de la concentración de Portugal ha generado un debate entre los tertulianos, aunque con diferentes lecturas sobre la responsabilidad del conflicto. María José Hostalrich señaló que "uno tiene que saber retirarse" y que el portugués "tiene una tendencia natural a marcharse mal de los sitios", mientras Manuel Martín pidió no responsabilizarle de todo: "Es muy fácil darle a Cristiano Ronaldo sin conocer el previo y sin conocer la figura de Jorge Jesús". Joan Prats consideró que el futbolista "tenía que haber sido más inteligente" y que, a estas alturas de su carrera, "era momento de respirar un poquito". Javi Estepa puso el foco en el seleccionador y recordó que "el daño que se le hace a Cristiano es más moral que deportivo". José Luis Allegue fue todavía más contundente al afirmar: "Estoy más en contra de la actitud de Jorge Jesús que en la actitud de Cristiano". Uno de los principales puntos de discusión fue la decisión de Jorge Jesús de hacer calentar a Cristiano durante media hora y finalmente no darle entrada. Hostalrich cuestionó que eso pueda considerarse una falta de respeto: "¿Por qué? ¿Por qué eso es una falta de respeto? Vamos a ver, es un entrenador, un seleccionador que trata de amarrar un resultado". Manu Martín, en cambio, recordó los antecedentes y defendió que "Cristiano Ronaldo después del Mundial y cuando nombran a Jorge Jesús le dice al seleccionador que deja la selección y Jorge Jesús le pide por favor que esté en las primeras convocatorias". Joan Prats insistió en que el episodio no le sorprendió: "Creo que a nadie nos sorprende ver a Cristiano actuar como actuó ayer". Estepa sostuvo que el seleccionador "no ha sabido tratar a Cristiano" y añadió: "No te puedes llevar a Cristiano teniéndolo ahí calentando media hora y no sacarlo". Allegue coincidió con esa lectura y afirmó que «nunca he visto, ya que estamos con las comparaciones, creo que jamás en mi vida he visto a Messi calentar media hora y no salir a un partido de fútbol». La gran incógnita ahora es si la ruptura puede reconducirse y si Cristiano tendrá una despedida acorde con su trayectoria internacional. Hostalrich cree que el episodio puede convertir su adiós "en una polémica más de su vida", mientras Manu Martín ve margen para una solución: "Puede que haya como mínimo un homenaje, un partido de despedida". Joan Prats considera que, pese a todo, el jugador "es una leyenda del fútbol" y que "es un jugador espectacular que ha trabajado una barbaridad para llegar a los 41 años como ha llegado futbolísticamente". Estepa, por su parte, ve el acercamiento "inviable" en este momento y apunta que Cristiano "cuando decida hablar, va a ir a de huello, va a ir a contar lo que él considera que es la verdad". Allegue, finalmente, reivindicó la dimensión histórica del portugués: "Es el mejor jugador de la historia de Portugal, uno de los mejores jugadores de la historia del fútbol y un tío que ha cambiado la historia de su país".

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: India win sailing, wrestling silver; cricket and hockey teams enter gold medal matches
articles.summary: India had a mixed but medal-filled day at the Asian Games on Thursday, winning silver medals in sailing and Greco-Roman wrestling while the defending
articles.body: India had a mixed but medal-filled day at the Asian Games on Thursday, winning silver medals in sailing and Greco-Roman wrestling while the defending champions in men's cricket and hockey reached their respective finals.India's medal tally rose to 65, including 10 gold, 23 silver and 32 bronze, keeping the country inside the top 10 of the standings.Sailing gives India early silverKerala cousins Prince Kurisinkal Noble and Manu Francis gave India an early medal in the men's skiff sailing event. The Indian pair finished second behind China and ahead of Hong Kong, China. They won one race and finished second in three of the nine races.It was India's first sailing medal of the ongoing Asian Games.India also won a bronze in the women's skiff event, with Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma finishing on the podium.Silver in Greco-Roman wrestlingIndia added another silver later in the day when Nitesh Siwach finished second in the men's 97kg Greco-Roman wrestling event.Siwach lost 0-4 to Japan's Yuri Nakazato in the final. A silver medal in Greco-Roman wrestling is a rare achievement for India at the Asian Games.Squash teams settle for bronzeBoth India's men's and women's squash teams ended their campaigns with bronze medals after losing their respective semifinals. The women's team of Anahat Singh, Joshana Chinappa, Tanvi Khanna and Shameena Riaz lost 1-2 to Hong Kong.Anahat, who had already won silver in the singles event, had four match points but could not close out her opening match against world No. 25 Sin Yuk Chan. She lost 2-3 (11-9, 11-8, 6-11, 11-13, 10-12).Tanvi then kept India's hopes alive with a 3-1 (4-11, 13-11, 11-9, 13-11) win over world No. 40 Ka Yi Lee. But veteran Joshana Chinappa lost in straight games to world No. 39 Ho Tze Lok, ending India's hopes of reaching the final.The defending champion men's team of Abhay Singh, Velavan Senthilkumar, Veer Chotrani and Suraj Chand also settled for bronze after a 1-2 loss to Malaysia.Ganesh adds another archery bronzeCompound archer Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru added a bronze medal to India's tally after winning his men's individual bronze medal match. Ganesh, who was part of India's gold-winning men's team on Wednesday, defeated Vietnam's Cong Duc Dang 149-144. The 20-year-old produced an excellent performance in the playoff, hitting the target with 14 of his 15 shots.Ganesh had lost 144-148 to South Korea's Kim Jongho in the semifinal. He went down 29-30, 29-30, 29-28, 29-30, 28-30.Cricket: India crush Sri LankaIndia's men's T20 team had little practice and game time before their semifinal against Sri Lanka. But none of that showed once the match began. Led by Shreyas Iyer, India posted 169/7 on a difficult pitch before bowling Sri Lanka out for just 45.Ishan Kishan played a key role with an unbeaten 80 off 46 balls, while pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah and Axar Patel took two wickets each.India now face Pakistan in the gold medal match after Pakistan beat Bangladesh in the other semifinal.Hockey: Abhishek saves India from Pakistan scareDefending champions India survived a huge scare against Pakistan before Abhishek scored with just 45 seconds left to seal a dramatic 4-3 win in the men's hockey semifinal.Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored from two penalty corners in the fifth and 13th minutes, while Sukhjeet Singh added a field goal in the 23rd minute. India looked in control at that stage, but Pakistan fought back strongly after the break.Abu Mahmood scored in the 30th minute, Hannan Shahid in the 45th and Waheed Rana in the 49th to bring Pakistan level.India struggled to regain control as Pakistan's forwards put the defending champions under sustained pressure.With the match heading towards a shootout, Abhishek produced the decisive moment in the final minute. His effort took a deflection off Pakistan defender Sufiyan and beat goalkeeper Ali Raza.India will face the winner of the other semifinal between South Korea and Malaysia in the final.Pranavi puts India in golf medal huntPranavi Urs produced one of the best rounds of the day in women's golf, shooting a seven-under 63 to move to second place. She is just two strokes behind leader Shannon Tan of Singapore.Pranavi began with back-to-back birdies and made four birdies in her first six holes. She then added three more birdies between the 13th and 16th holes. She completed the round without dropping a shot. Her performance also lifted India to the bronze-medal position in the women's team event, with India at seven-under 273.Diksha Dagar is T-21st after rounds of 71 and 73, while Aditi Ashok is T-25th after scores of 71 and 74. The best two scores from each round count towards the team medal.India assured of sepaktakraw medalIndia secured at least a bronze medal in men's quadrant sepaktakraw after reaching the semifinals. India beat Myanmar 2-1 to finish unbeaten and top Group A. India won 10-15, 15-13, 15-7 after earlier victories over Laos and Vietnam. They had beaten Vietnam 2-0 (15-12, 15-9) earlier in the day. The semifinals will be played on Friday.Tennis campaign ends without a medalIndia's tennis team will return from the Asian Games without a medal for the first time since 1986.Sumit Nagal's quarterfinal exit in men's singles brought the Indian tennis campaign to an end. Nagal lost 4-6, 4-6 to China's Yibing Wu in one hour and 38 minutes on Thursday.Indian judokas, cyclists and pistol shooter Anish Bhanwala also missed out on medals after making early exits from their respective events.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Yankees without Aaron Judge showed why this might be their best chance to win with him
articles.summary: As the New York Yankees’ young ace Cam Schlittler mowed down Boston Red Sox batters in a way that felt not only effective but deliciously vindictive, chants of “M-V-P!” rained down from the Bronx crowd.
articles.body: As the New York Yankees’ young ace Cam Schlittler mowed down Boston Red Sox batters in a way that felt not only effective but deliciously vindictive, chants of “M-V-P!” rained down from the Bronx crowd. There was a tinge of hometown bias to the honorific, but not enough to call it hyperbole. It was also a key sign of what’s different about these Bronx Bombers from past seasons. Schlittler, the New England native now pitching in enemy territory, will almost certainly win the American League Cy Young award for his sub-2.00 ERA in his first full season. Playoff appearances don’t factor into awards voting, but Game 1 of the American League Wild Card Series was more than worthy. Schlittler is at his best in a big moment – especially if there’s the chance to piss off a bunch of his former fellow Bostonians. And so he did that and the fans declared him the most valuable in return. “I mean, we already got an MVP in this locker room. He’s won three of them,” Schlittler demurred when asked about the cheers after the Yankees’ first victory of the series. A dutiful deference to the captain. Even sidelined with a calf injury, Aaron Judge loomed large as the Yankees embarked on the run that they hope ends in a 28th World Series title. His absence from the introductions became a source of speculation on social media. Any incremental update to his status was fodder for pre-game questions even with a playoff series on the line. The hyper focus is merited. Judge is arguably the greatest power hitter the game has ever seen. He has those three MVP awards Schlittler mentioned. The first was won the same year Schlittler was drafted out of Boston’s Northeastern College (Judge was Rookie of the Year while Schlittler was still rooting for the Red Sox in high school in Weymouth, Massachusetts) and the third was won just last season. This year, the Yankees had the best offense in the AL before Judge was placed on the injured list with a rib fracture at the end of May; they were bottom three the remainder of the season largely without him. “If he were in there this whole season, he’d probably have it,” Schlitter concluded of Judge and the award some fans say he deserves instead. Perhaps. It’s easy to understand how it might be sacrilege to suggest otherwise within these hallowed halls. The Yankees are an organization of icons, of men who became monuments. And maybe they will still erect a monument to Judge that mentions the 2026 season – but not for what he’s accomplished so far this year. If he has a hero moment on a bigger stage later this month, it will be because the rest of the team didn’t need him to get there. In a routing, rousing, definitive sweep of the Red Sox in the wild card, the current iteration of the Yankees looked like the best chance the team has had to win it all with Judge. They looked like that because they won without him. The stats from earlier this season, which suggested it would have probably been a successful – but not quite superlative – year for Judge, matter less than a simple fact: Judge will be 35 next year and he has already been great for nearly a decade. This is not to say that he is washed or his prime wasted. The Yankees have won a lot in the Aaron Judge era. They won because of Judge. In a sport that generally rewards complete, deep teams, Judge looks like someone who could carry a whole club himself and the Yankees’ results supported that supposition. Except when it matters most. The Yankees haven’t won the World Series in 17 years and MLB’s most famous franchise would like you know that, in a sport with 30 teams, their drought has left fans the thirstiest. It’s not because Judge can’t hack it in October – he hit .500 last postseason and the Yankees didn’t make it out of the division series – but it turns out there’s no conversion rate between individual accolades and championship rings. It’s possible – just possible – that Aaron Judge’s peak years are behind him. He is the venerated veteran in a clubhouse getting younger in a way no individual human ever can. The Yankees put another 6-foot-7 superman in right field (Spencer Jones), only this one never saw a second of the 20th century, which is maybe why he can turn a strikeout into a six-run rally through sheer hustle. They have a different power hitter who competes for the home run title and has a six-RBI night to open the postseason (Ben Rice), and this one went from being drafted out of an Ivy League school in the 12th round to leading off for the Bronx Bombers. In Game 2 against Boston, New York had a starting lineup in which every guy got a hit and all but one scored a run. They didn’t need them all because they also have the best starting rotation in the sport. The further into October they play, the more likely it is that the Yankees will get Judge back, potentially as soon as the division series on Saturday. They routed their longtime nemesis – outscoring the Red Sox 18-2 – and now they’ll face the winner of their division, a modern rival and a study in contrasts, in the Tampa Bay Rays. If Judge is on the roster for that series, it’ll be tempting to say the Yankees survived without him. But they didn’t, they thrived. “We got a young, hungry team here that’s excited for the postseason,” Judge himself said, sticky with champagne amid the celebration that followed the sweep. “A lot of guys in their first postseason, so they’re excited to put on the show.” This is still his team. They’re still better off with him healthy and contributing on the field. Any team would be. But Judge understands the effort it takes just to get a team to the stage where heroes are made. This year, the rest of the team had to carry him. All the more reason to make the most of it. “I’m going to play this game for a short amount of time and you only get so many opportunities to enjoy this with your friends and throw champagne around a clubhouse and spray people with beer,” he explained about why he kept the goggles propped atop his head even as the booze burned his eyes. He said it makes him feel young. “Every single time.”

articles.title: El Real Madrid asegura a la gran promesa de la Selección Colombia: firmó hasta 2030
articles.standfirst: Gorka Abascal renueva con el Real Madrid: contrato con el club 'merengue' hasta 2030
articles.summary: Gorka Abascal renueva con el Real Madrid: contrato con el club 'merengue' hasta 2030
articles.body: El Real Madrid sigue blindando a sus promesas de cara al futuro y esta vez el turno fue para una de las jóvenes figuras con proyección internacional: Gorka Abascal, atacante con nacionalidad colombiana y española, firmó una extensión de contrato con el club merengue hasta el año 2030. Nacido en Bilbao pero de madre colombiana, Abascal cuenta con la doble nacionalidad que le permite representar a ambos países. Sin embargo, el jugador ha tomado la decisión firme de vestir la camiseta tricolor de la Selección Colombia, integrándose en los procesos juveniles dirigidos por el director técnico Fredy Hurtado en la categoría Sub-17. El canterano forma parte de la camada de talentos emergentes de la Tricolor junto a nombres como Santiago Vallecilla, Éider Carrillo, Miguel Agámez y José Escorcia, quienes apuntan a liderar el recambio generacional del fútbol colombiano. Con esta renovación, el Real Madrid ratifica su confianza en el desarrollo del volante de La Fábrica, asegurando su permanencia durante la etapa clave de su transición al fútbol profesional. Para el año 2030, cuando se dispute el Mundial de la FIFA en España, Portugal y Marruecos, Abascal alcanzará los 20 años de edad, proyectándose como una de las piezas jóvenes a seguir tanto a nivel de clubes en Europa como en el entorno de la Selección Colombia absoluta.

articles.title: Tesla tenía que ser: por primera vez un eléctrico es el coche más vendido de España
articles.standfirst: La marca de Elon Musk consiguió el liderato de ventas en septiembre con su Model 3
articles.summary: La marca de Elon Musk consiguió el liderato de ventas en septiembre con su Model 3
articles.body: Tenía que ser Tesla. La marca de Elon Musk ha conseguido un nuevo hito en España: convertir a uno de sus coches, el Model 3, en el coche más vendido en nuestro país en el mes de septiembre. La berlina eléctrica americana ha destronado al Dacia Sandero, tradicional dominador del mercado español (y, de hecho, el coche más vendido en lo que va de año, con diferencia) y también al Seat Ibiza, que en septiembre consiguió también batir al compacto rumano. Tesla colocó 2.528 unidades de su Model 3 frente a los 2.183 Ibiza y los 2.157 Sandero. Además de ser la primera vez que Tesla logra encabezar un ranking de ventas en España... también es la primera vez que un coche eléctrico ocupa este puesto de honor. En lo que va de año 2026 el liderazgo indiscutible es para el Sandero, que ha sido elegido ya por 25.926 clientes, frente a los 22.020 que han optado por el Seat Ibiza y los 19.257 del Toyota Corolla. Precisamente la japonesa es la líder del mercado también en septiembre, con 9.172 entregas, casi el doble que el segundo (Renault, con 5.551) El 'efecto Tesla' ha conseguido que el peso de los coches eléctricos se dispare en nuestro país. En septiembre los modelos de baterías fueron la segunda tecnología de propulsión más solicitada y, de hecho, los eléctricos puros supusieron el 16,3% de las ventas (frente al 10,3% que suponen en todo lo que va de año).

articles.title: Super League Grand Final: Will 2026 finally be the year Warrington Wolves win at Old Trafford?
articles.summary: Can Super League's perennial nearly side Warrington Wolves get over the line and win a first Grand Final this Saturday?
articles.body:
Britain did not have a single motorway in 1955.

We were still five years out from the MOT being introduced and cars did not require a seatbelt.

There was one television channel, provided by the BBC.

The humble postcode had not yet been rolled out across the land.

And rationing was still very much in the national memory, having only been phased out a year beforehand.

All of this paints a picture as to what life was like when Warrington last won a league championship.

On Saturday they stand 80 minutes away from ending a 71-year wait for another title and their boss Sam Burgess has the chance to lay down a marker as a coach just as he did during an illustrious playing career.

But can Super League's perennial nearly side finally get over the line and finally earn a league triumph in the modern era?

Quiz: Name every Super League Grand Finalist

Two Wembley defeats - now Old Trafford awaits

Former England captain Burgess began his career as Warrington head coach in earnest ahead of the 2024 season - off the back of Daryl Powell's uncompetitive stint in charge of the Wire.

A legend of the game as a player, it was his first top job as a coach, five years after he retired following his enviable stint both on the pitch and as assistant coach down under with South Sydney Rabbitohs.

A first Wembley appearance came shortly after, as Wolves reached that season's Challenge Cup final, when they were undone by a Wigan Warriors side on the way to a quadruple.

Twelve months later, treble-winners-in-waiting Hull KR beat them again in the final.

Burgess' side eventually missed out on a play-off spot altogether in 2025, finishing eighth, but, in contrast, they have put together a consistent campaign in 2026 to finish third in the table, behind second-placed Leeds on points difference.

So you might expect Burgess to be feeling rather pleased with himself, and his side, as they prepare for the first Grand Final of his tenure and a meeting with Powell, who has inspired Wakefield's ascent from the Championship to the top of the sport after leaving the Wire.

"Not really," Burgess replied when asked in his pre-match media commitments whether it gave him extra satisfaction that his side had proved him right by emerging as challengers after their disappointing 2025.

"I'm pretty satisfied to be here. I guess I'll find out how satisfied I am on Saturday at about eight o'clock."

Listen to commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra, BBC Radio Merseyside, BBC Radio Leeds and BBC Sounds; watch highlights Saturday, 3 October from 23:00 BST on iPlayer and BBC Two on Sunday at 13:45 BST

It took 14 years into the Super League era before Warrington reached their first Grand Final and this year is the fifth time they have reached Old Trafford, following previous finals in 2012, 2013, 2016 and 2018.

Tony Smith's impressive Wire side came undone against Leeds first and then again at the hands of Wigan in 2013 and 2016 - with Steve Price last leading the club to a Grand Final in 2018 when they were defeated by the Warriors for a third time in a row.

Since that point, the Primrose and Blue have failed to trouble the upper echelons of the sport, with St Helens' dominant spell starting the following year while Wigan and Hull KR have both taken turns at having a commanding stint of their own.

So far this year, they have narrowly missed out on second place in the regular season and dispatched reigning champions Hull KR and Leeds in the play-offs.

Yet when times were tough in 2025, Burgess never gave up and said that it was a belief in his side and the knowledge that Warrington had a long-term plan that kept his camp motivated.

"I could see a lot of green shoots last year where we're going," he added.

"You've got to be able to believe it to do it, and I believed in the club, I believed in the players we had, and I believed in the philosophy that we've got, so I guess we've been very consistent all year without jumping out at anyone, which is a good sign.

"We've had a lot of challenges throughout the year, we've managed them well as a club, which has been important."

Ask those in the know at the beginning of the 2026 season which two teams would contest the Grand Final and not many would have picked out Warrington or Wakefield.

"It's Warrington's year" has become something of a meme in the northern hemisphere's rugby league fandom in the past few years - describing how one of the league's best-funded and well-supported teams always looks the part, but falls at the final hurdle.

Former England coach Steve McNamara arrived at the club as an assistant coach last October following his departure from a spell at Catalans, who he guided to the Challenge Cup and two Super League Grand Finals.

He is set to join Hull FC for next season but Burgess believes their previous failures have not happened in a vacuum - but have shaped the team they have become this season.

"We've played a couple of big games over the last three years, so we've got a bit of experience," said Burgess.

"We have matured as a group and as a club. The club has matured with us, which is important. Whether it counts as much, on Saturday, we'll see."

Of course, Burgess' time as a player can be summed up by a stunning 2014 season which culminated in a victorious NRL Grand Final with the Rabbitohs, when he played on with a broken cheekbone and also won the Clive Churchill Medal as man of the match.

Asked about how he reflected on that moment ahead of his first Grand Final as a coach, Burgess said: "It's much easier as a player.

"Any experience is experience whether it's as a player, coach, staff member, assistant, whatever. We've got a bit of experience in the room.

"Steve McNamara brought a lot of experience to us this year as well, which is going to help for something.

"We've got a lot of things in our corner. Again, when the whistle blows at six o'clock, you've got to do the right jobs and get the performance on the field."

articles.title: Aarón Sánchez: entrenar, estudiar, trabajar… y llegar a ser campeón del mundo
articles.standfirst: El español participará este fin de semana en el Campeonato de Europa de Stand up Paddle
articles.summary: El español participará este fin de semana en el Campeonato de Europa de Stand up Paddle
articles.body: Aarón Sánchez tiene 22 años y lleva 15 sobre una tabla. Encontró muy pronto su pasión y desde entonces buena parte de su vida se ha organizado alrededor del mar. Hoy es campeón del mundo pero detrás del título hay muchas horas de trabajo y renuncias que nunca aparecen en una clasificación: «He sido muy afortunado. Mi familia, mi club y mis amigos siempre han entendido lo que supone el sacrificio de un deportista de alto nivel», explica. Y cuando habla de sacrificios no piensa únicamente en grandes decisiones: «Son los pequeños detalles: entender que tienes que faltar a un evento importante, ayudarte en la recuperación o facilitarte las cosas para poder entrenar». Durante años, Aarón ha compaginado entrenamientos y competiciones con los estudios y, en algunas etapas, también con trabajos a media jornada. El bodyboard es un deporte minoritario que continúa creciendo, pero alcanzar una estabilidad económica que permita dedicarse exclusivamente a competir no siempre resulta sencillo. En ese camino tampoco quiso dejar de formarse. Acaba de graduarse en Ciencias de la Actividad Física y del Deporte: «Siempre hemos combinado el deporte con los estudios. Hay etapas en las que estudias más y otras en las que entrenas más». En su caso, además, ambas facetas terminaron encontrándose: estudiar deporte mientras intentaba llegar cada vez más lejos como deportista. El título mundial conseguido el pasado año cambió algunas cosas. Por primera vez puede dedicar todo su tiempo al deporte después de temporadas en las que tuvo que entrenar, estudiar y trabajar al mismo tiempo. Ahora disfruta de esa oportunidad pero no olvida lo que hubo antes ni a quienes hicieron posible el camino. Aarón insiste en que detrás de cualquier deportista hay muchas horas que el público nunca llega a ver. Y también muchos jóvenes que, pese a las dificultades, continúan entrenando cada día buscando una oportunidad. Después de quince años, él ha conseguido la suya: «Trabajo duro y pasión. Para mí son lo más importante. Uno tiene que ir de la mano del otro». Aarón participará este fin de semana en el Campeonato de Europa de Stand up Paddle, dentro de la competición de los Juegos del Agua organizada por ADESP, la Asociación del Deporte Español, junto a 11 Federaciones Deportivas Españolas en la Ciudad Autónoma de Melilla.

articles.title: Luke Littler: Phil Taylor and Barry Hearn both warn world No 1 to 'get used to boos' after mixed reception at recent tournaments
articles.summary: Darts legend Phil Taylor and sports promoter Barry Hearn give words of advice to Luke Littler with the world No 1 subject to boos and whistling in recent tournaments; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton from November 14-22 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 ended at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam where he complained about being repeatedly whistled by Dutch supporters.

The back-to-back world champion even threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled by the vociferous crowd.

Taylor, a 16-time world champion, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after winning his final world crown and he backed Littler to turn the boo-boys in his favour.

Speaking to Sky Sports News , Taylor said: "Littler has got to get used to the boos. Go in there and turn the crowd. Sometimes if you play well and you start hitting your 140s and 180s, your big finishes, the crowd will turn and don't react to it, but he does react.

"He's young and he's a little bit cocky at times but that's good, that's confidence. He's just got to accept crowds are going to be on his back for a little bit, but they will get bored with it.

"Keep doing what you're doing, keep playing well, and just concentrate. Let them boo and then do your little antics when you've won."

He continued: "Littler doesn't have responsibilities. He can just go up there and enjoy himself and win tournaments. Go up there, enjoy it, take no notice of the crowd, which isn't easy, obviously, but work out a way of turning the crowd around."

Taylor also discussed how Littler would have improved his game "100 per cent" and advised the Warrington phenom to continue playing the board.

"I would have loved him to have been about," said 66-year-old Taylor. "Any player that used to come through I used to love anyway because I looked at ways of raising my game.

"You have to be a bit like Rocky Balboa by getting the chicken out and chasing it down the garden. It's great to see him up there and he's a lovely lad who is not money orientated.

"Players that were better than me, I thrived on it. I loved it."

Taylor added: "What players are doing now is that they're watching him and they're jumping on him. Players are getting used to him and they will improve, which will put more mental pressure on Luke.

"He might then think, 'I need to practise a bit more,' so he's doing things to improve his game whereas before he's going in there and not thinking about it."

Taylor was also asked whether anybody could match or even overtake his phenomenal record of world titles. He said: "To win 16 world titles you've got to be very professional and you've got to do it for at least 25 years, I'd say.

"It will be very difficult to match me but whoever has got talent can do it."

Hearn: Littler needs to show people boos won't affect his game

Barry Hearn, former chairman of the Professional Darts Corporation, says Littler wants to show people that the boos will not put him off his game.

"In my view, he's a natural-born darts player," Hearn told Sky Sports News . "He's making a huge amount of money. He's changing his family's life and generations beyond, which is what all sports stars should aim for. He is the best in the world, clearly.

"His record says that. He is 19 and his schedule is something that needs delicate managing and he's got a good team behind him to make sure he achieves that.

"And he will get booed and frankly, when was the last time you saw a penalty being taken in the home end by the visitors? Was it quiet or did they boo? You've got to get used to this sort of thing. It's part and parcel of being a professional.

"Of course, we hope and try to encourage the crowd to show decent order, but there are times when you're in someone else's back garden."

Hearn pointed to the fact Peter Manley and Gerwyn Price both suffered from continuous booing in the past, but eventually won the crowd over.

"It's happened to a lot of players over the years. Manley was the first one I came into contact with, but of late, Price got a lot of stick. He smiled back at them and today, he's one of the world's most popular players. Luke has got to concentrate on that more, showing that it doesn't affect him," said Hearn.

"He's good enough to show that he can still win and that basically will keep the boo boys, who are out of order by the way, without doubt, keep them quiet."

articles.title: WNBA reveals why A'ja Wilson was not ejected for approaching Fever fan during playoff game
articles.summary: Aces star A'ja Wilson avoided ejection against the Fever because officials ruled she stood in a player escape lane during the fan confrontation.
articles.body: Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson wasn’t ejected for confronting an Indiana Fever fan during Game 2 of their WNBA first-round playoff series because officials determined she remained in an area beside the basket that they considered part of the court area, OutKick has learned. Following an in-game review during Tuesday’s Aces-Fever playoff game, officials concluded that Wilson was in a player escape lane adjacent to the basket stanchion. That determination was the basis for allowing the Las Vegas star to remain in the game, according to a league source. The WNBA also reviewed the incident and found that the fan had not violated its Fan Code of Conduct. OutKick asked the league whether Wilson would face additional discipline, including a fine or suspension, but did not receive an answer to that question before publication. The Athletic reported Thursday that Wilson would not face further league discipline and would be available for Game 3 against the Fever. PRIME VIDEO WNBA BROADCAST CREW EMBARRASSES ITSELF WITH COVERAGE OF A'JA WILSON FAN INCIDENT The explanation addresses a question OutKick raised with the league after the confrontation: Why wasn’t Wilson ejected under a rule requiring players to be removed for deliberately entering the stands? Rule 12A, Section V, subsection l(4) of the 2026 WNBA Official Rule Book requires an ejection for "Deliberately entering the stands other than as a continuance of play." The rulebook’s player conduct section also specifies where the stands begin. "The first row of seats is considered the beginning of the stands." Despite Wilson walking into an area where fans were seated, officials determined that she had remained in the court area. They classified the space she occupied as a player escape lane rather than part of the stands, according to the league source. Wilson received a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct following the fourth-quarter incident at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. She approached the fan near the baseline, and teammates intervened during the confrontation. Afterward, Wilson defended her reaction, saying she believed the fan had stepped toward her and pointed at her. "I don’t give a damn what you said. I don’t give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable," Wilson said. She also apologized to her teammates for receiving the technical. The Fever had already determined that the spectator had not broken the arena’s rules. In a postgame statement, the team said security personnel had spoken with the fan and witnesses, found no code-of-conduct violation and considered the matter closed. There is an important distinction between additional discipline and the standard consequences of a technical foul. The rulebook provides for fines for unsportsmanlike technical fouls. It also gives the commissioner discretion to impose a fine or suspension regardless of whether a player was ejected. In other words, the game officials’ ruling on Wilson’s location did not prevent the league from imposing additional punishment. articles.title: Melilla presume de mar y deporte con Radio MARCA
articles.standfirst: Espectacular día con 'El Programa de Ortega' en los Juegos del Agua
articles.summary: Espectacular día con 'El Programa de Ortega' en los Juegos del Agua
articles.body: El Programa de Ortega vivió una tarde especial desde la espectacular Ensenada de los Galápagos con motivo de los II Juegos del Agua, con Juan José Imbroda, Feliciano López, José Hidalgo, presidente de ADESP, Miguel Ángel Fernández Bonnemaisón, Miguel Ángel Rozas, Juan Ramón López Caro, Luis Carrión, Rafa Sanz y Goyo Jiménez como protagonistas. Melilla presumió de mar, deporte y de uno de sus rincones más espectaculares de la mano de Radio MARCA. El Programa de Ortega trasladó su emisión hasta la Playa de la Ensenada de los Galápagos, donde Vicente Ortega y su equipo realizaron dos horas de radio en directo, de 17.00 a 19.00 horas, para acercar a los oyentes toda la dimensión de los II Juegos del Agua. La cita, que se celebra entre el 26 de septiembre y el 18 de octubre, reúne durante 23 días a más de 3.000 participantes, entre deportistas, técnicos, jueces y personal de organización. Con 11 federaciones deportivas, nueve campeonatos, dos exhibiciones y cuatro sedes, los Juegos del Agua han convertido Melilla en uno de los grandes epicentros nacionales de los deportes acuáticos, aunando competición, sostenibilidad y promoción turística. La importancia del evento para la ciudad fue uno de los grandes asuntos de la tarde. Juan José Imbroda, presidente de la Ciudad Autónoma de Melilla, y Miguel Ángel Fernández Bonnemaisón, consejero de Educación, Juventud y Deporte, pasaron por El Programa de Ortega para explicar la apuesta de Melilla por una cita que trasciende la competición y que pretende dejar también un importante legado económico, social y turístico. "Es la ciudad que más invierte en deporte en España en función del número de habitantes. El deporte es la mejor imagen y estos Juegos del Agua nos ponen otra vez en el mapa", aseguró un Imbroda, que se emocionó al recordar a su hermano Javier. "Era un crack, siempre decía que había que alejarse de los tristes y disfrutar de la vida". Por su parte, el consejero Fernández Bonnemaisón afirmó que "El deporte es la mayor herramienta para la difusión de la ciudad", aseguró el consejero, que vive con ilusión estos II Juegos del Agua "Todas las federaciones han creído en este proyecto", señaló. La ADESP impulsa un evento que se vive en todos los rincones de la ciudad como explicó José Hidalgo, su presidente. "Tenía que ser en Melilla por el paraje y porque es un pabellón azul que une el cielo y el entorno. Melilla es una gran desconocida", reflejó. El deporte fue otro de los grandes protagonistas con la presencia de Miguel Ángel Rozas, campeón de España de Aguas Abiertas, que compartió su experiencia y acercó a los oyentes una de las disciplinas que mejor representan la estrecha relación de Melilla con el mar. Los Juegos cuentan, además, con dos referentes del deporte español como embajadores: Mario Mola e Iballa Ruano. Y en Melilla se forja una gran campeona en Halterofilia como Salma Tahiri, campeona de España a sus 19 años. También hubo tiempo para los recuerdos de la mano de dos ex entrenadores de la UD Melilla como Juan Ramón López Caro, que recordó Melilla como "una de las ciudades que recuerdo con más cariño" y apostó Por Rodri como Balón de Oro y Luis Carrión, que disputó aquella recordada eliminatoria de Copa del Rey ante el Real Madrid en 2018. Y una de las grandes sorpresas de la tarde llegó con el ex tenista Feliciano López, que se inició en el circuito en Melilla porque su padre se encontraba destinado allí. "Hasta los 10 años estuve dando guerra en Melilla. Tengo muchos recuerdos", recordó al tiempo de hablar de que el tenis español "parece un milagro" por poder disfrutar de Nadal, Alcaraz o Rafa Jódar. Otro de los clásicos de Melilla es el baloncesto y el histórico Ciudad de Melilla, que milita en la 2ª FEB y que entrena Rafa Sanz y que sueña con el ascenso y con que la gente vuelva a ilusionarse en la ciudad con el deporte de la canasta. Y en una tarde dedicada a Melilla no podía faltar uno de sus rostros más conocidos. Goyo Jiménez, natural de la ciudad, también se pasó por El Programa de Ortega y puso el toque de humor a una emisión muy especial. El humorista habló de su tierra y compartió con Radio MARCA una jornada en la que Melilla pudo mostrar al resto de España algunos de sus grandes atractivos. La Ensenada de los Galápagos, el Mediterráneo y los Juegos del Agua fueron el escenario perfecto para una nueva salida de Radio MARCA. Una tarde en la que deporte, entretenimiento y ciudad se dieron la mano para mostrar una Melilla volcada con el deporte y orgullosa de su vínculo con el mar a todo el Universo MARCA.

articles.title: Libaak y Alfonso se meten en cuartos de final en Rotterdam y apuntan al Mundial
articles.standfirst: El revés y el drive argentinos superan un exigente cruce ante Leal y Guerrero y presentan sus credenciales para la lista albiceleste de cara a la cita de Qatar
articles.summary: El revés y el drive argentinos superan un exigente cruce ante Leal y Guerrero y presentan sus credenciales para la lista albiceleste de cara a la cita de Qatar
articles.body: Mientras la selección española ya ha hecho oficial su lista de convocados para el Mundial de Doha que se celebrará la primera semana de noviembre, la selección argentina aún no ha anunciado los ocho jugadores que representarán al combinado albiceleste. Con varios puestos perfilados por ranking, las últimas plazas de la convocatoria cuentan con diversos candidatos, entre los que Valentino Libaak y Gonzalo Alfonso han presentado una firme candidatura tras su rendimiento en el Rotterdam P2. Alfonso pelea por un puesto en la posición de revés junto a perfiles como el de Juan Tello. En los octavos de final en tierras neerlandesas, la dupla argentina se midió a Javi Leal y Fran Guerrero, recientes campeones del FIP Platinum de Lyon. El choque comenzó con ventaja para Libaak y Alfonso al adjudicarse la primera manga por 7-5. Aunque Leal y Guerrero reaccionaron para igualar el encuentro en el segundo set, la pareja argentina volvió a imponer su juego en la tercera y definitiva manga para certificar la victoria y el pase a la siguiente ronda con un 6-4. El triunfo clasifica a Libaak y Alfonso para sus segundos cuartos de final como proyecto conjunto, confirmando las buenas sensaciones mostradas tras alcanzar las semifinales en el P1 de Madrid y manteniéndose firmes en la pugna por entrar en la lista definitiva de Argentina. En el cuadro femenino, la jornada estuvo marcada por la retirada por lesión de Carmen Goenaga durante su compromiso junto a Bea Caldera frente a Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo. Tras disputarse los tres primeros juegos del encuentro, con ventaja de 3-0 para las cabezas de serie número cuatro, Goenaga solicitó la asistencia y comunicó la imposibilidad de continuar en pista. A la espera de pruebas médicas que determinen el alcance de las molestias y su disponibilidad para los siguientes compromisos de la gira europea, Goenaga y Caldera se despiden de la cita neerlandesa de forma prematura. Por su parte, la unión circunstancial entre Claudia Jensen y la joven española Claudia Escacena saldó con éxito su debut. Ante la baja por lesión de Tamara Icardo, la jugadora argentina recurrió a Escacena para asegurar su participación en el torneo, logrando acceder a los cuartos de final y sumando unos puntos valiosos para mantener su posición en el ranking FIP.

articles.title: Mike Norvell's seat is hot, but he could still save his job
articles.summary: FSU head coach Mike Norvell is still on the hot seat with a 2-2 start. However, he can still save his job if the Seminoles go on a string of wins.
articles.body:
Florida State just hasn't lived up to the program's standards over the last few seasons. Since the 2023 season, the Seminoles have a record of 9-19 with a dreadful 3-14 mark in the ACC. Currently, they're 2-2, and they have a very tough conference schedule over the next two months, starting with the Virginia Cavaliers on Saturday.

Mike Norvell is the one who has all eyes on him for these failures as the head coach. The seat he's sitting on is hot. In fact, it's scorching, and it will only get worse if FSU keeps losing games. With that said, according to John Talty of CBS Sports , Norvell can still turn things around with a plethora of wins.

Since the season started, Florida State has fired its AD, suffered a bizarre power outage in its home opener, and has stumbled to a 2-2 record. There's a path to Mike Norvell keeping his job, but it almost certainly needs to include a win over Virginia this weekend. Norvell needs to be in that 7-win range and still has games against Louisville , Miami and Florida on the schedule. With an athletic department in transition, a $46.7 million buyout is still a huge sum to pay out, and it could help Norvell's cause if he can get a few more wins. If Norvell can win two of the next three (UVA, Louisville, Miami) before the bye, there's a viable path to survival.

Norvell is generally seen as a very nice guy and someone that people gravitate to, especially his players. Those are great qualities for a person to have, but football is a results business, and Florida State isn't producing the amount of wins it needs to. Until that happens, Norvell will continue to feel the pressure from the Seminoles fan base, and he should.

There's also the Jimbo Fisher factor. It was reported a few weeks ago that FSU is exploring the possibility of bringing him back if things don't turn around. That possibility will become even more appealing if Norvell has his fifth losing season in seven years.

Time will tell how this all plays out. However, one thing is for certain: Norvell needs to win if he wants to remain the head coach at Florida State.

articles.title: Why starting Aaron Nola over Zack Wheeler will cost Phillies series vs. Braves
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies fought to give themselves one more chance. Now, with their season on the line Thursday night in Atlanta, they are handing the ball...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies fought to give themselves one more chance. Now, with their season on the line Thursday night in Atlanta , they are handing the ball to Aaron Nola instead of Zack Wheeler .

Phillies fans are praying that decision doesn't undo everything their team accomplished to force a deciding Game 3.

Philadelphia survived Wednesday with a 4-3 victory in 10 innings, powered by home runs from Bryce Harper , Kyle Schwarber , and Alec Bohm . The offense delivered when it looked like another quiet night would have sent the Phillies home.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Wheeler started Sunday's regular-season finale, meaning a start Thursday night would come on three days' rest. That really isn't a concern. An elimination game demands a different approach: All hands on deck. The pitcher who gives Philadelphia the best chance to survive tonight is Wheeler, despite him never pitching on short rest once in his career.

"If I am Wheeler, I am walking into that office and taking the ball for Game 3," CC Sabathia said on Peacock's postgame show on Wednesday night.

He has been one of baseball's premier starters over the past decade, and his ability to control a game makes him the pitcher Philadelphia should want facing Atlanta's lineup first. His 2026 season has included difficult stretches, but the trust he has earned does not disappear because Nola has an extra day to recover.

Wheeler just demonstrated that value Sunday, allowing one run over six innings as Philadelphia clinched its postseason berth. He already helped save the season once this week. Asking him to do it again would come with risk, but there is also risk in watching Atlanta build an early lead against someone else.

Nola deserves a fair assessment here. He posted a 3.33 ERA in the second half, so this is not a decision to start a pitcher who has been ineffective for months. His susceptibility to home runs, however, remains a concern when one swing could decide the series.

The argument for Wheeler is about which veteran deserves the first opportunity to dictate the game. Nola can still deliver five strong innings and make this criticism look foolish. But if he struggles immediately, the Phillies could spend the rest of the night trying to recover from a decision they cannot take back.

Mattingly's preference comes down to rest. Wheeler threw 97 pitches Sunday and could still appear in relief Thursday. That possibility matters, because starting Nola does not necessarily mean leaving Wheeler out of the game.

Still, using Wheeler after trouble develops is a different assignment from letting him establish control from the opening pitch. If Mattingly trusts him to handle a critical relief appearance, there is a reasonable argument for trusting him with a shortened start, then adjusting from there.

Wheeler has the second-best WHIP in postseason history at 0.72. What he has been able to do at this level is why you need to trust him in this game over Nola.

A victory would send Philadelphia to face the Los Angeles Dodgers at Dodger Stadium, where the rotation could be rearranged again. Nola might have been an option to open that series had Wheeler started Thursday. Those plans only matter if the Phillies advance.

With the season hanging on one game, he should have chosen the pitcher he could trust most. If the Braves end the Phillies' season tonight, that distinction will follow this decision well into the offseason.

articles.summary: Colorado hosts No. 10 Texas Tech looking to end a two-game losing streak. Buffaloes Wire staff predicts and gives thoughts on Saturday's matchup.
articles.body:
Colorado hosts No. 10 Texas Tech for its Big 12 home opener, with the Buffaloes hoping to right the ship after back-to-back Power Four losses.

The key for the Buffs remains the same: stop the self-inflicted wounds. Penalties, turnovers and other mental mistakes have stalled otherwise positive offensive drives. Not to mention, the quarterback play has been less than stellar, leading to Deion Sanders reportedly making a change at the position heading into Saturday's game.

In the last two weeks, only four of 27 offensive drives have resulted in points, and 10 have ended in a turnover, including several on failed fourth-down conversions. The Buffs are the lowest-scoring offense in the Big 12 (21.5 points per game) despite averaging 400 yards per game and ranking in the middle of the conference in total yardage.

Colorado is close to a two-touchdown home underdog against Texas Tech, suggesting a win will be hard to come by. The Buffaloes have the talent to pull off a top-10 upset, but they need to put it all together, especially on offense.

With just a couple of days until kickoff, here are our Buffaloes Wire staff predictions for Colorado's Week 5 matchup vs. Texas Tech.

While I don't expect Texas Tech to put up many points, the Red Raiders will still win dominantly. Texas Tech does not have the most impressive offense, but their defense is on another level. Especially with how Colorado has struggled offensively against every Power Four team this season, they will not be able to get much going against this defense. Texas Tech quarterback Will Hammond will probably turn the ball over once, since he has five interceptions in the first four games, and the short field could give the Buffaloes a chance to get in the end zone. Still, this game won't be competitive. Texas Tech's defense will win the game and force a turnover or two.

Colorado can give Texas Tech problems if it gets back to the running game and executes a few deep shots for Isaac Wilson. The Buffaloes need Micah Welch, JaQuail Smith and the offensive line to avoid putting Wilson in constant long-yardage situations. Texas Tech has allowed passing yardage this season, and Colorado needs a big game from Joseph Williams, Quanell Farrakhan Jr. and Kam Perry to have a chance. The Buffaloes should play better at Folsom Field, but Texas Tech, with running backs J'Koby Williams and Cameron Dickey, will control the game.

Last week, I thought Texas Tech looked very beatable against Sam Houston, and the Red Raiders are definitely worse than they were a year ago. However, Colorado hasn't shown anything offensively that suggests they can score enough to pull off an upset. Isaac Wilson should help get the Go-Go offense going, but beating Texas Tech requires controlling the clock with the ground game and taking advantage of a quarterback in Will Hammond, who has shown he will turn the ball over. As Colorado knows well, short fields lead to scoring opportunities, and if the Buffs' defense can manufacture a few, CU's offense won't have to do much. Ultimately, I still think Texas Tech is too big of a challenge for this version of Colorado, but it won't be a blowout.

articles.title: Josh McDaniels Offers More Details About Drake Maye's Shoulder Injury
articles.summary: The Patriots offensive coordinator shed some light on what Maye is dealing with ahead of Week 4.
articles.body:
The Patriots know they need to bring their best to knock off the undefeated Bills on the road. That's one reason why an injury report appearance this week for Drake Maye raised plenty of concern for fans.

Maye downplayed the issue on Wednesday, telling reporters he "wouldn't say there is a problem," but any sign that the 24-year-old is playing at less than 100 percent is enough to sound the alarm for some.

On Thursday, Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels shed some more light on what Maye is dealing with. Here's what you need to know.

McDaniels downplayed Maye's injury, telling reporters that it's been "business as usual" in practice and claiming the issue hasn't affected the quarterback's confidence.

Maye first appeared on the injury report Wednesday with a shoulder issue, but he was listed as a full participant in practice.

The Patriots offensive coordinator confirmed Maye suffered the injury against the Jaguars, when he was "dinged," so it wasn't an issue in either of the first two weeks of the season.

McDaniels said the injury won't impact his pay-calling against the Bills on Sunday, adding that the ailment is just the result of taking routine hits.

"He's always been a guy that can run and do things with his legs and all that. He's taken a few hits since he's been in the National Football League," McDaniels said. "That's part of the process when you can make things happen with your legs. You're going to incur some hits."

articles.title: How LSU transfer Joel Rogers found his fit with UTSA
articles.summary: Though a spring shoulder injury threatened to slow his transition, LSU transfer Joel Rogers has found a role at safety in his first year at UTSA.
articles.body:
Less than a week into spring practice at his new home, UTSA safety Joel Rogers suffered a torn labrum and a dislocated shoulder, triggering a monthslong absence.

A former four-star recruit, Rogers had already been forced to wait longer than he wanted for his chance on defense, relegated mostly to special teams through his first two years at LSU.

A transfer to UTSA offered a path to more playing opportunities, until the injury presented another roadblock. But while coach Jeff Traylor suggested the transition might have been even smoother with more practice time, Rogers has proven ready to hit the ground running this fall, delivering the game-sealing interception in Saturday's win against Colorado State while steadily expanding his role in the defense.

"I went from being kind of down after transferring, which wasn't any bad terms leaving LSU, but I just felt like I wanted more playing time," Rogers said. "Having a coach that trusts in me and believes in me, and then getting the opportunity to show that. Once I show it, teammates believe in me, and it feels big. It's like bouncing back."

Though he ranks 12th on UTSA's defense in snaps played, per Pro Football Focus, Rogers is fourth on the team in tackles, racking up 18 stops. He also snared his first career interception in Saturday's 59-45 win over the Rams , charging forward to slide in front of a pass up the right sideline in the closing minutes.

Traylor said he expects Rogers "will only continue to get better" as he gains more experience following the time lost to injury.

"He pressed through it. Super kid. I'm thrilled," Traylor said. "He just loves football and wants to play. He loves to tackle. He reminds me of some other great safeties we've had here, with how much he loves football."

Rogers said he knew how to handle rehabbing his shoulder after suffering a similar injury earlier in his career, but that didn't make the setback any less frustrating.

"There was a point where I had to really think within myself like, 'What am I doing this for?'" Rogers said. "It's still a new start, even though things didn't go how I wanted to. I'm in a new spot. So as soon as I got back, it's like, 'OK, how can I get back to being me, get back to playing ball?'"

That process started when he jumped back into workouts at the beginning of preseason camp, catching up on the defensive system while rounding back into shape.

Rogers was fighting to secure a significant role on defense for the first time since his days at West Feliciana High in Louisiana, as he played just 15 defensive snaps across two seasons at LSU. He was more involved in the special teams last year with the Tigers, playing on the coverage and return teams for both kicks and punts as he said he was doing "whatever I could to get on the field."

"I feel like I didn't get what I was expecting coming out of high school," Rogers said. "I had to make a decision to where I could go somewhere and feel like I knew I could play immediately, and then start getting to showcase what I could do."

He was projected for a more glamorous role coming out of high school, as 247Sports ranked him as a four-star prospect and the No. 27 safety in the country. Rogers remembers having a difficult time sorting through all the phone calls from various programs that expressed interest. In the modern era, finding a fit is about not just the scheme, coaches and environment, but also the financial possibilities, too.

He found the play at LSU to be fast paced and "just a different level of football."

The shift to UTSA has given him a fresh opportunity.

"I just want to be a football player. I want to show what I can do," Rogers said. "I have a lot of God-given abilities, so I just want to be able to showcase that."

articles.title: Rangers place Joonas Korpisalo on IR, recall Dylan Garand for backup duties
articles.summary: Just two games into the regular season, the Rangers’ goaltender depth is already being put to the test.
articles.body:
Just two games into the regular season, the Rangers ' goalie depth is already being put to the test.

Joonas Korpisalo is week-to-week with a lower-body injury, and has landed on IR.

Korpisalo was expected to come in and serve as the top option behind star starter Igor Shesterkin after being acquired from the Bruins in an offseason deal.

With him sidelined, Dylan Garand has been recalled from Hartford.

Garand, of course, was viewed as the favorite to slide into the No. 2 spot before the Korpisalo deal.

The youngster still had a chance to compete for a spot in camp, but he ended up landing on waivers late last week.

Upon clearing, Garand was assigned to Hartford.

Instead of starting the season as their top option between the pipes, though, he now receives another opportunity to show what he can do at the pro level.

The 24-year-old impressed in his first cup of coffee at the pro level last season, allowing two or less goals in his three appearances down the stretch.

Garand will likely play Friday against Detroit on the second night of a back-to-back.

articles.summary: Falcons DT Gervon Dexter made one thing clear after inking 4-year extension..
articles.body:
"Just getting started," Falcons defensive tackle Gervon Dexter wrote on social media upon signing a four-year, $78 million contract extension that will keep him Atlanta through the 2030 NFL season.

The former second-round pick spent his first three years with the Chicago Bears but was traded to the Falcons at the start of the 2026 season.

Atlanta had been looking for another dominant interior defensive tackle since letting Grady Jarrett sign with the Bears in 2025, and the team appears to have found one in Dexter.

The 24-year-old has made quite an impression over his first three games in Atlanta. Dexter currently leads all defensive tackles in QB pressure rate (20.5%), and has helped the Falcons become the NFL's No. 1 run defense.

The Falcons have another budding star in third-year defensive tackle Brandon Dorlus , who continues to improve as the team surrounds him with more talent.

Between Dexter, Dorlus, Maason Smith , Cameron Thomas and LaCale London , Atlanta's defensive line rotation looks promising for the future.

"Gervon is a young, ascending talent whose power, disruption and impact along the defensive line are difficult to find," Falcons GM Ian Cunningham said of Dexter's extension. "What's been just as impressive is the growth he's shown off the field as a man and a father."

The defense should only continue to improve when the team gets both Jalon Walker (ACL injury) and James Pearce Jr. (suspended) back in the lineup.

articles.title: “I Don’t Want to Give My Honest Answer” – Willson Contreras Gets Real About Red Sox Issues After Yankees Send Them Out of Wild Card
articles.summary: Willson Contreras shared his honest take on the Boston Red Sox’s shortcomings after their Wild Card sweep by the New York Yankees, pointing to areas the team...
articles.body:
Willson Contreras shared his honest take on the Boston Red Sox 's shortcomings after their Wild Card sweep by the New York Yankees , pointing to areas the team must improve.

The Red Sox were eliminated from the 2026 MLB postseason after the Yankees swept them 2-0 in the American League Wild Card Series. The Yankees dominated the best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium, outscoring Boston 18-2 across the two games. In Game 1, the Yankees shut out Boston 9-0 behind a strong performance from Cam Schlittler , who threw 6.1 scoreless innings.

In Game 2, Max Fried dominated for six innings before the Red Sox briefly found some momentum when Contreras hit a solo home run in the sixth inning, snapping Boston's 26-inning postseason scoring drought. However, the Yankees quickly regained control and eventually secured a 9-2 victory to complete the sweep. Following the loss, Contreras shared his honest response during the postgame locker room interview.

When asked about what went wrong with the Red Sox offense down the stretch of the regular season and into the playoffs, he said:

"I'm not gonna answer it because, I don't wanna give my honest answer, but, we got eliminated, that's the bottom line. We got in here trying to win. We didn't produce, we didn't execute any part of the game, and that's why we lose. I mean, I know that we had a really good stretch," said Willson Contreras.

"I'm really proud of what we did in the past, like I said, we were able to turn the season around for sure, 100%, but that's not enough. It's not enough, and at the end of the day, you win games in the regular season to clinch the playoffs, but then falling short in the playoffs, it's tough."

Despite the disappointing ending, the 2026 season was a rollercoaster for Boston. After a 32-46 start that left them at the bottom of the AL, the team went on a historic second-half surge to secure a playoff berth.

What did Willson Contreras say after the Red Sox clinched a spot in the 2026 playoffs?

The Boston Red Sox clinched an American League Wild Card spot in the 2026 MLB playoffs on Sept. 20. Despite losing 5-1 to the Tampa Bay Rays , they secured a postseason berth after the Atlanta Braves defeated the Houston Astros . The Astros' loss officially eliminated them from contention and secured Boston's playoff spot.

Following the achievement, Willson Contreras reflected on the team's remarkable turnaround in an interview. Expressing his pride in the team and his belief in his teammates, he said:

"I'm really thankful, first of all, for playing for Boston. Thankful for the front office for asking me to come here and all of the good human beings that are here on this team. This is just the first step ahead. I just wanted to let everybody know that I'm proud of every one of you," said Willson Contreras.

"I did believe in my team. I did believe in everybody who was here. I never had a doubt that this team couldn't turn the season around. At one point, we were texting each other and I just said, 'Keep believing in ourselves.'"

Contreras played as a first baseman and designated hitter for the Red Sox in 2026, setting career highs in home runs and RBIs. He played 130 games during the regular season, recording 123 hits and 68 runs.

articles.title: Caleb Douglas in danger of missing second straight game for Miami Dolphins
articles.summary: Douglas has yet to practice since injuring his ankle late in week two loss.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had a debut for the ages — nabbing five passes for 94 yards against the Las Vegas Raiders in week one. Unfortunately, the young player suffered an ankle injury in the fourth-quarter of Miami's week two loss to the San Francisco 49ers . He was seen in a walking boot following the game and eventually missed the team's tilt against the Kansas City Chiefs at home in week three.

According to David Furones of the Sun Sentinel, Douglas was not seen practicing for the Dolphins on Thursday — continuing the recent trend of missed practices for the rookie while he recovers from his ankle ailment. That puts his availability for Miami's week four contest on the road against the Minnesota Vikings in serious jeopardy despite head coach Jeff Hafley's early week optimism while labeling Douglas as "day-to-day."

In his absence last week, fellow rookie receiver Chris Bell led all Dolphins' receivers in receiving yards — tallying 67 yards on four receptions. Malik Washington added five receptions for 56 yards.

Going against a Brian Flores led Vikings defense, quarterback Malik Willis could benefit greatly from Douglas's separation skills. After all, Douglas led the NFL in separation yards per route run after his week one showing — averaging 5.3 yards of separation each time he ran a route. Unfortunately, it looks like Willis, and all Miami Dolphins' fans, will likely have to wait at least one more week to see Douglas back in action.

articles.title: Napheesa Collier unsure what her future with Minnesota holds
articles.summary: Collier is set to become a free agent, meaning the 2019 first-round pick's run with the Lynx could be coming to an end.
articles.body:
Napheesa Collier may have played her last game with the Minnesota Lynx .

The 30-year-old WNBA star is set to become an unrestricted free agent, and it remains unclear whether she and Minnesota are interested in reuniting in 2027 after this year's team finished No. 1 in the regular season only to get swept by the eighth-seeded New York Liberty in the first round of the playoffs.

During Thursday's season-ending press conference, Collier said she hasn't had much time to think about what's next.

"Honestly, I haven't even thought about that. We lost less than 48 hours ago. We didn't expect to be here, you know?" Collier said. "I really haven't had any time to decompress or anything like that. I can tell you I love it here; I love the organization; I love my team and everything like that, but I just haven't had the time to give that any thought."

When she does start to think about what's next, she'll be talking to her family.

"Speaking to your family, speaking to everyone, and by doing what feels right for you. That's not something I'm thinking about right now by any means, but I think, just generally, in a process where you're making a big decision, those are the factors that go into it," Collier said.

Collier set herself up for free agency when she settled for a one-year, supermax contract ($1.4 million) with the Lynx earlier this year. She could've signed a multi-year deal like other WNBA stars did, à la A'ja Wilson's three-year deal with the Las Vegas Aces .

That doesn't mean she won't be back with Minnesota, but this would've been a non-factor had she signed with the Lynx for multiple years. If the Lynx do make her a compelling offer to re-sign, they'll do so under the impression that she'll return to the form that made her an MVP runner-up in 2024 and 2025.

Collier's 2026 season was limited to 16 regular-season games after ankle surgeries in January and March, respectively, kept her from debuting until July 22. She averaged 16.8 points and 6.9 rebounds, well below the 22.9 points she averaged in 2025 and the 9.7 rebounds she averaged in 2024.

"I feel confident that I'll be able to get back to my normal 100 (percent)," Collier said Thursday. "Just getting back to that baseline and exceeding that is my goal, and I have every confidence that it's going to happen."

If Collier returns, the Lynx could have the same starting five: Collier with Olivia Miles, Kayla McBride , Courtney Williams , and Natasha Howard , the latter four of whom are all under contract with Minnesota in 2027.

articles.title: ARE WE HAVING FUN YET
articles.summary: How can fans find joy amid the anxiety?
articles.body:
I love the film Moneyball for a lot of reasons, but one part of the film really resonates now.

If you recall, Billy Beane's life was baseball — once as a player and, as the movie starts, as the general manager for the Athletics .

But he doesn't watch the games. At first pitch, he might be working out in the gym. He might go for a drive. But sit in the stadium and watch every excruciating pitch? No way.

Well, I never played baseball and nothing in my personal life depends on the outcome of the Rays postseason and yet….when the postseason starts I feel so stressed that I can barely watch.

When it's a series against a rival like the Yankees I'm nearly comatose with anxiety. The pain of losing to THOSE guys – with their air of entitlement, the sense that the world begins and ends with them. Their stupid minor league stadium dimensions (and then their fans griping if an opponent actually beats them shooting "home runs" to the short porch); their acting like they are better than the rest of us but then using a b-tier electronics store jingle ad to signify a strikeout. The thousands of New Yorkers who flee their region to enjoy OUR weather and OUR low taxes while continuing to root for the Yankees, and who then boast that they outnumber the Rays fans (which they don't by the way, they are just very loud and obnoxious) when in fact they have priced long time Floridians out of the region.

Oh and by the way did I mention, I'm from New York City? So I really am entitled to call these folks out.

I thought baseball was the thing I did to escape the difficult parts of life. Work can be stressful, family can be complicated, there are fires and floods everywhere, so of course we turn to baseball, that traditional, pastoral sport for escape.

When we get to the postseason, however, it's the baseball part that seems stressful.

In 2023 I decided to address this by going all in on participation. I bought tickets for all the Wild Card games (of which just two were played), got a new postseason shirt, cleared my work schedule and immersed myself in the game. And I was rewarded with the two worst Rays games I've ever seen, and I was around for the Devil Rays .

This year I've decided to stay home (clearly I was the bad luck charm) and I'm looking for ways to get into the right mindset to actually, you know, enjoy baseball. Ice cream? Meditation, with my new mantra: "Any October baseball is good. Any October baseball is good."

Or maybe alcohol. I've created a drinking game where I take a shot every time someone — baseball folks, random fans on social media — says some variation of "who are these guys?" Double shots if a ball hits a catwalk. I invite you to join me, or if you aren't a drinker substitute your substance of choice.

I also line up all my Rays swag and bobbleheads around my TV and light a few candles. That should surely help.

And if things get tense, well, I'll go to the store.

Where are you on the anxiety-to-joy continuum? What is your strategy for dealing with the many Yankee fans certain to cast a dark shadow over the Trop this week?

He was named tournament MVP and earned All-Star Five honors after his standout performance, including a near triple-double in the championship game against China with 26 points, 10 rebounds, and nine assists.

articles.title: Michael Jordan's 1997 Ferrari with Air Jordan connection sells for eye watering sum
articles.summary: Rare Ferrari tied to Bulls legend sets new public auction record for the model.
articles.body:
A luxury car once owned by Michael Jordan has sold for an eye-watering amount.

The custom Ferrari 550 Maranello previously owned by the Chicago Bulls legend sold for $2.7 million on Wednesday via Pharrell William's auction house JOOPITER.

Only 3,083 models were built between 1996 and 2001.

The sales price blew past the auction house's estimate and set a new public-auction record for the model, according to JOOPITER.

The Ferrari attracted 43 bids, which isn't surprising due to its one-of-a-kind connection to Jordan.

Jordan purchased the Rosso Barchetta-colored car in 1997 in the middle of his championship run with the Bulls. Weeks later, he was spotted leaving the United Center in the car after winning his fifth NBA title.

Michael Jordan's Ferrari inspired the Air Jordan 14

The Ferrari had a significant connection to the NBA legend's Air Jordan sneaker line.

Nike designer Tinker Hatfield once used the custom Ferrari as inspiration for the Air Jordan 14.

In addition to serving as an inspo for shoes, the vehicle was unique in several other ways.

It featured custom seat tracks to accommodate Jordan's 6-foot-6 frame.

According to the auction listing, "Ferrari is understood to have extended the seat rails and specified slimmer-than-standard padding, allowing the seating position to be set as far back as possible. The specification remains one of the rarest and most elegant offered on the 550 Maranello: Rosso Barchetta over tan leather."

Jordan sold the car in 2002, and it basically disappeared from public view for nearly 24 years before being rediscovered.

John Temerian, co-founder of vintage car preservation company Curated, reportedly purchased the luxury car from the long-term California owner in May.
