For much of the night at the Estádio da Luz, FC Bayern Women 's patience was severely tested. Benfica defended passionately, and the Munich side rarely managed to find a way through the tightly organised defence. But the game turned in the closing stages: Klara Bühl broke the deadlock with a powerful finish from distance, and Pernille Harder added a second shortly afterwards, crowning the evening with her 50th Champions League goal. When Franziska Kett made it 3–0 in the 88th minute, it wrapped up the first win of the season nicely – a late, hard-fought victory that was all the more valuable for it.

Join us behind the scenes in Portugal: from the final team meetings and arriving fully focused at the Estádio da Luz, through the tension before kick-off, to the looks of relief after the final whistle. You'll see not only the joy of this crucial away win, but also the quiet moments in between – brief glances, hugs and the pride of securing three hard-fought points on the big European stage.

The Chicago Cubs recently saw their season come to an end with a 4-1 loss in Game 2 of the Wild Card round against the San Diego Padres , resulting in a sweep loss in the series. The Cubs now face an offseason filled with more questions than answers after a season filled with much promise and championship potential ended with a dud.

The MVP of the Cubs, and likely the NL, this year was Pete Crow-Armstrong , who put together one of the most dominant seasons in recent MLB history for his work in 2026.

However, now, Cubs insider Patrick Mooney of The Athletic has hit the team with a stern warning as the offseason gets underway.

"Looking ahead, the Cubs shouldn't assume that Crow-Armstrong will stay on this trajectory and remain a superstar into the next decade… hoping that Crow-Armstrong will annually produce once-in-a-lifetime seasons that elevate the entire operation is not a strategy," he noted.

Indeed, while there's certainly no reason to think that PCA will be taking a step back anytime soon, banking on him to produce at an MVP level year after year in order to keep the team above water is not a great approach for future success.

Mooney also noted that "The Cubs will have a lot of work to do this offseason, before and after the widely anticipated lockout. Beyond Happ and Suzuki, primary catcher Carson Kelly is on the verge of free agency, the entire season-ending rotation may need to be replaced and the Cubs still don't have a closer."

Clearly, the Chicago front office will have its hands full this offseason as they look to piece together what went wrong in the playoffs.

articles.title: Make No Mistake, Caleb Durbin Was No Red Sox Success Story This Season
articles.summary: Most considered Caleb Durbin to be a fine contributor to the Boston Red Sox this season. He wasn't.
articles.body:
If there's one undeniable quality Craig Breslow has demonstrated, it's his ability to prematurely declare victory on personnel moves.

It happened last year when Breslow nearly dislocated his elbow patting himself on the back over signing rookie Kristian Campbell to an extension, only for Campbell to fall into a months-long slump that led to him spending all of this season in Triple-A. Then it happened this year, with Breslow and the rest of the Boston Red Sox brass all but taunting their own fans over younger, cheaper third baseman Caleb Durbin apparently outperforming Alex Bregman and Rafael Devers , Durbin's predecessors in the hot corner at Fenway Park.

Although Durbin cooled off at the plate after a strong June, the general opinion of the 26-year-old's play this season was that his sterling glove and solid, though not spectacular, bat provided value to a squad that fit the former 14th-round pick's scrappy persona. Had he indeed provided both of those things, then it's a useful balance. The problem is, that wasn't the case at all.

While Durbin was excellent defensively, in the end he chipped in very little offensively. With the Red Sox eliminated after Wednesday's Game 2 loss to the New York Yankees in the AL Wild Card Series, it can be definitively stated that what Durbin gave the Red Sox this season honestly wasn't good enough.

The overall numbers tell a mixed story. He batted .248 with a .332 on-base percentage and slugged .378. He hit 13 home runs and stole 20 bases. As middling as those statistics are, somehow he compiled 4.4 WAR under Baseball Reference's criteria, which is the number his defenders will cling to. Considering how slowly Durbin got started, the fact that he was able to raise his batting average to almost .250 is a credit to him, isn't it?

Rather than Durbin's poor start being an outlier in an overall successful season, in fact the few scorching weeks he used to pull his stats back to respectability were the the outliers , while the struggles were the norm. He posted a .963 OPS in June and hit six home runs -- 46% of his season total -- in that same month. Burrowing down further, the bulk of his production came during a pair of two-week stretches from May 28 to June 10 and June 18 to June 30. In the former, he went 15-for-44 (.340) in his at-bats. In the latter, he went 19-for-45 (.422)! He collected more than a quarter of his total hits in less than a month's worth of games.

None of this should have been surprising, except perhaps to the analytics-averse players in the Red Sox clubhouse. Durbin never has made good contact or hit the ball hard. Batters of that nature -- like Durbin's partner on the left side of the infield, Trevor Story -- are prone to hot streaks when their dying quails happen to fall where the fielder's aren't. But producing offense through weak contact isn't sustainable.

In layman's terms, Durbin hits with a wet rolled-up newspaper. In scientific terms, Durbin was at the bottom of the league in exit velocity at 83.1 mph and in hard-hit percentage at 25%. His bat speed is in the bottom 12%. His 88% whiff rate might be shrugged off if he complemented the swings and misses with the occasional dinger, but alas.

These aren't acceptable numbers for a corner infielder who plays half his games at Fenway Park. A third baseman on a successful Red Sox team needs to be regularly above an .800 OPS, either by slashing base hits like Bill Mueller and Wade Boggs or being a long-ball threat like Devers and Mike Lowell. The pattern to pitching Durbin has developed: crank fastballs that he can't catch up to. And there's frankly no use to a right-handed corner infielder who can't hit a fastball over the Green Monster.

Durbin is a nice complementary player. If he played second base, he might even be considered valuable. But after a mediocre first season in Boston that was far worse than most fans are willing to admit, Durbin has done nothing to exorcise the demons of the infamous Devers trade or the decision not to re-sign Bregman. If anything, he's confirmation of just how much the Red Sox need a hitter of their caliber -- and how difficult it is to find a replacement when you let not only one but two get away.

articles.title: Darts' World Grand Prix: Format, results and prize money
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything explains how Darts' World Grand Prix works ahead of the start of the 2026 tournament
articles.body:
The 2026 Darts World Grand Prix starts on Monday, 28 September and is one of the Professional Darts Corporation's major titles.

Unlike the rest of the sport's majors, the tournament uses a 'double in, double out' format.

The 32 players featuring are made up of the 16 best-ranked players from the PDC's Order of Merit, and the best 16 from the past 12 months via the Order of Merit who had not already qualified.

A total prize fund of £750,000 is up for grabs, with the winner earning £150,000.

Teenager and current world number one Luke Littler was the winner in 2025, cruising to a 6-1 victory over Luke Humphries in the final.

But he was knocked out in the opening round by Luke Woodhouse in 2026.

The 'double in, double out' darts format presents a big twist to the gameplay.

It means that a player must start all legs on a double, rather than on any scoring zone on the board.

The use of 'double in, double out' has been in use in the World Grand Prix since its inaugural year in 1998.

The format is in set play, with each set being the best of five legs.

The first round is a best-of-three-sets match, increasing to five sets in the second round.

The quarter-finals stay at the best of five sets, before an increase to nine sets in the semi-finals.

The final is a best-of-11 match, also described as a race to six sets.

(5) Jonny Clayton 3-1 Wessel Nijman (12)

(5) Jonny Clayton 2-1 Krzysztof Ratajski

(3) Gian van Veen 2-0 Dirk van Duijvenbode

The prize money for the whole tournament has increased to £750,000 this year, an increase of 25% from last year's £600,000.

The winner will take home £150,000 instead of the £120,000 jackpot 12 months ago. Barring the prize money given to players who lose in the first round, every other value has also increased.

Who has previously won the World Grand Prix?

Phil Taylor is the most successful player in World Grand Prix history, winning the tournament 11 times.

Michael van Gerwen is the next most successful player with six titles, with James Wade (twice) being the only other player to win it multiple times.

The World Grand Prix has produced six different winners in the last six years.

articles.title: Texas 2026 Schedule Re-Rank: Who is toughest Longhorns opponent left?
articles.summary: Now that a third of 2026 season is over, we take another look at rest of the Longhorns schedule to see which games are easier and which are tougher.
articles.body:
Over the summer, we took a good look at the Texas Longhorns schedule. We ranked all of the UT opponents from easiest to hardest, highlighted three very dangerous games and three games Texas must win . But with a third of the season in the books, a few things have changed.

A big change from preseason is that Texas is now the No. 1 team in the nation. The Longhorns have vanquished Ohio State , the then No. 1 team, at home in Austin. The Horns also held on against No. 14 ranked Tennessee in Knoxville.

At the beginning of the season, there were seven ranked teams on UT's schedule. There are still seven, but a few of the teams have switched.

The struggles of Texas A&M and Oklahoma have seen both teams fall from the preseason top ten all the way out of the Top 25. But Mississippi State and Florida are both much better than anyone anticipated and have taken the place of the Longhorns rivals in the poll.

The Longhorns only have one game left against a team that hasn't been ranked at all in 2026.

Here is a re-ranking of the remaining Longhorns opponents now that we have a better sense of the quality of each team:

8. Arkansas Razorbacks in Austin on Nov. 21

Analysis : The Hogs move up a spot only because Texas has played four games and two of the teams UT has played where higher on the original list (Tennessee and Ohio State). Mississippi State has leaped over the Razorbacks from our original ranking.

Arkansas is the worst team remaining on the Longhorns schedule. The Razorbacks have wins over North Alabama and Tulsa, but the Hogs were dominated by Georgia and Utah. The game at A&M this week should be interesting.

7. Oklahoma Sooners in Dallas on Oct. 10

Analysis : Most experts thought the Sooners would be as good, if not better, than last season that saw the Sooners make the College Football Playoff. Something Texas didn't do. OU was 9-3 last year, with losses to Texas, Ole Miss and Alabama in the CFP.

But the Sooners are not as good as last year, especially quarterback John Mateer . The Sooners were beaten by a very suspect Michigan team and where humiliated at Georgia last week. OU barely beat lowly New Mexico in Week 2. We listed the Red River Shootout as a must-win game in the preseason and that's even more true now since the Sooners have been abject through four games.

6. Missouri Tigers in Columbia on Nov. 11

Analysis : The Tigers are roughly what they were at the beginning of the season. There was an expectation Missouri would be undefeated right now, but the Tigers ran into a much-improved Mississippi State team last week. Mizzou's schedule is about to get a lot tougher, starting with Florida on Saturday.

Mizzou is still ranked, the game is still in Columbia, so this is no gimme for the Horns.

5. Texas A&M Aggies in College Station on Nov. 27

Analysis : Like they have in the polls, the Aggies have plummeted down this list. Almost no team in college football has choked on its expectations more than the Aggies. A&M's rough first half against Arizona State wasn't an aberration, it was a warning of things to come. The Ags have been beaten at home by Kentucky and were destroyed by LSU over the past two weeks.

The Lone Star Shootout will still be a difficult date for Texas. The Aggies are still the Horns biggest rivals and the game is still on the road with 100,000 Aggie fans screaming hatred at UT. But it is hard to imagine QB Marcel Reed and the Texas A&M offense having much, if any, success against the Texas defense.

4. Mississippi State Bulldogs in Austin on Oct. 31

Analysis : This is Texas' third season in the SEC and the Bulldogs have been conference cellar dwellers for most of that period. But not this year. Behind sophomore QB Kamario Taylor , Hail State is one of the best stories in college football this season.

Texas struggled against the Bulldogs last year, needing overtime to vanquish Mississippi State. The 2025 Longhorns were still finding their footing when they visited Starkville. UT gets Hail State in Austin this year, but the Bulldogs are much better.

Analysis : The Rebels are a top ten team this year and have one huge win under their belt, beating LSU at home in Week 3. But Ole Miss was also humbled in the Swamp against Florida last Saturday.

Mississippi is a very good SEC team with possibly the best quarterback in the nation in Trinidad Chambliss . If you have a good quarterback, you can compete against anyone. This is a dangerous game for Texas. Coming out of the OU game, the Longhorns play five ranked opponents in a row. The Ole Miss game could be pivotal.

Analysis : LSU could be very good by the time Texas travels to Death Valley. The Tigers lost to Ole Miss in a revenge game for the Rebels, who were jilted by coach Lane Kiffin in the offseason. LSU walked into a hornets nest and got stung.

But the Tigers looked dominant in their win against Texas A&M at home last week. Tiger Stadium is one of the toughest places to play in the nation and, no matter how good the Longhorns defense is, Kiffin will find ways to score.

Analysis : Florida has been the most impressive team in the SEC, besides Georgia. New coach Jon Sumrall has revived a traditional power that has been dormant for almost a decade. Florida has crushed all four of its opponents this season, including an impressive blowout of Ole Miss last week.

The Longhorns have struggled with Florida since joining the SEC, even though the Gators have been down. In 2024, UT had to pull away late to shake Florida in Austin. And we all know what happened last year. The Horns went into the Swamp and where manhandled. That loss is the biggest reason Texas missed the CFP.

Texas catches a break that the game is in Austin. But Florida looks like one of the best teams in the nation. This game is only two weeks from now and if both teams hold serve, it will be one of the most-hyped and most dangerous games on the Longhorns schedule.

articles.title: Manchester City breaches need tax implication answers, UK Parliament told
articles.summary: HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) has been contacted in the United Kingdom about Man City’s financial breaches.
articles.body:
The fallout from the Manchester City case reached the United Kingdom Parliament on Thursday, with ⁠⁠the Treasury Committee chair asking Britain’s tax authority to report on measures taken in response to the Premier League’s findings.

The request comes after the Premier League said Manchester City used “sham” commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and ⁠understate costs by more than £900 million ($1.2bn) over nearly a decade.

Committee chair Meg Hillier said ⁠⁠she had written to His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC) Permanent Secretary JP Marks after the publication on Tuesday of the independent commission ruling that the club had committed “well over 100 individual ⁠⁠breaches of the Premier League Rules across the course of many seasons”.

In her letter, Hillier sought assurances that HMRC was “seized of the importance” of the findings and questioned the tax authority about its response.

She asked whether HMRC was aware of the commission’s ‌‌findings, whether it had requested or been provided with an unredacted copy of the report and what assessments it had made of any potential tax implications arising from the case.

HMRC can unpick a company’s tax returns and reject contrived transactions that reduce the company’s taxable income. HMRC can also apply financial penalties for underpaid taxes as a result of false ⁠⁠statements.

However, City’s actions would have ⁠⁠artificially inflated the company’s profitability, which would have increased their taxes.

“I would also welcome an overview of current HMRC work around ⁠⁠football clubs,” she concluded. “I would be interested in ⁠⁠any common issues around taxation (including the taxation of remuneration) that you have found in their practices, and how HMRC is tackling them.”

Manchester City did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Hillier’s intervention broadens ‌‌the fallout from the case, which has already prompted debate over possible sanctions, the appeals process and potential compensation claims by rival clubs and players.

Manchester City have ‌‌denied ‌‌wrongdoing and are expected to lodge an appeal against the commission’s findings before Friday’s deadline.

articles.title: Protesters halt game as calls grow on Ireland to boycott second Israel game
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland’s game halted by tennis balls thrown and invader with Palestine flags amid Israel boycott demand.
articles.body:
Protesters against Ireland playing its Nations League games against Israel interrupted the team’s match against Austria on Thursday by throwing tennis balls onto the field.

Referee Allard Lindhout sent the players for a hydration break as soon as the balls bearing Palestinian flags landed on the grass with Ireland 1-0 up after 19 minutes played.

Troy Parrott had opened the scoring in the 12th with a brilliant individual goal, playing the ball through the legs of one defender and then eluding another before shooting the ball through the goalkeeper’s legs.

The game resumed after a four-minute break, after which it flipped with Austria in the ascendancy until Parrott made it 2-0 with a penalty — in off the right post before the break.

Before that, a man had tried running onto the field but was stopped by stewards. Irish broadcaster RTE reported he was carrying a Palestinian flag.

Protesters also gathered before the match because of Israel’s actions in Gaza. A small group of campaigners from the “Stop the Game” initiative set up close to the stadium and displayed a Palestinian flag and banners in support of Ireland player Gavin Bazunu, who decided on Saturday to boycott both of his team’s matches against Israel.

The Ireland Palestine Solidarity Campaign organised a protest outside the stadium, as well as others around the country.

They’re calling for Ireland to boycott its remaining Nations League match against Israel — Ireland’s “home” game, though it’s set to be played without any fans present in Backa Topola, Serbia on Sunday.

The Football Association of Ireland moved the game to a neutral venue for “operational reasons” in June following widespread calls for a boycott. It also followed the FAI’s own motion the previous November calling on UEFA to ban Israel from club and international competitions.

The “Stop the Game” initiative, which on Wednesday issued an open letter to the squad and its coach Heimir Hallgrimsson asking them not to play on Sunday, has also asked the Irish government and FAI to cancel the game.

Ireland already played Israel’s “home” game in Debrecen, Hungary last Sunday, when the Irish players wore black armbands and scored three first-half goals to win 3-0.

The players deliberated for hours the day before as to whether they should play at all, after Bazunu informed the coach that morning that he wished to withdraw from both games.

FAI chief executive David Courell said the players voted and that “a significant majority” were in favour of playing. Widespread reports suggested the vote was 14-8 in favour, excluding Bazunu, who had already departed.

Bazunu, Ireland’s reserve goalkeeper, was back in the squad for Austria’s visit.

Finn Azaz, whose mother has Israeli heritage, was back in the team after being left out against Israel.

The Irish team has been under increasing pressure in their home country, where affinity with Palestinians is strong, to boycott playing against Israel.

The FAI has resisted the calls, arguing the team could be hit with punishing sanctions by UEFA. Ireland is cohosting the 2028 European Championship with England, Wales and Scotland.

articles.title: Joy for Germany and Klopp as Ronaldo-less Portugal win in Denmark
articles.summary: Jurgen Klopp secures first win as Germany manager, while Cristiano Ronaldo’s absence not felt by Portugal in Austria.
articles.body:
Germany claimed a ‌first win under new coach Juergen Klopp on Thursday with a 2-0 Nations League victory ⁠over Serbia, while Portugal ⁠shrugged off the absence of Cristiano Ronaldo in Denmark and the Netherlands came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Greece.

Klopp selected a completely new starting XI from ⁠the side that lost to Greece last time, handing debuts to goalkeeper Jonas Urbig and winger Derry Scherhant.

Germany attacked the Serbia goal in waves, but it took until the 39th minute to take ⁠the lead as Florian Wirtz picked out Tom Bischof to score his first senior national team goal in his second cap.

After Nick Woltemade missed a sitter at the back post, Wirtz scored the second just past the hour-mark with a neat finish from the edge of the box.

There will be relief for Klopp to ‌get a win at the third attempt on his return to coaching, and his side were full value for their victory.

Greece were close to making it three wins from three but conceded a late equaliser at home to the Netherlands.

Fotis Ioannidis and Giorgios Masouras scored first-half goals for the home side, before Virgil van Dijk halved the deficit just before the hour-mark.

The visitors kept pushing for the goal and it arrived a minute from the end via Tijjani Reijnders.

Portugal – playing their ⁠first game since Ronaldo walked out on the squad, putting his international future ⁠into doubt – were made to work for their 4-2 win in Denmark as they top A4 with a perfect nine points from their three games.

The visitors scored twice in the first half through Joao Cancelo and Goncalo Ramos, but on each ⁠occasion the Danes found an equaliser as Mikkel Damsgaard and Rasmus Hojlund netted for the hosts.

But Portugal would not be denied. Vitinha grabbed a 67th-minute ⁠goal and Joao Felix a late fourth to give Jorge ⁠Jesus’ side a six-point lead in the table after what has been a difficult few days.

Dan James and Neco Williams scored for Wales as they beat 10-man Norway 2-1 to earn their first points of the campaign.

In League B, the clash between Ireland ‌and Austria in Dublin was stopped briefly when tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch in protest at the Irish side playing Israel in their previous fixture.

Play soon resumed and Ireland were held to a ‌2-2 ‌draw as a pair of goals from Troy Parrott was not enough for the win.

Ireland’s next game is a ‘home’ clash against Israel that will be played behind closed doors in neutral Serbia.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight confirmed, but is the bout too late?
articles.summary: As Fury and Joshua confirm long-awaited boxing fight, Al Jazeera explains the delays and exchanges between the sides.
articles.body:
When Tyson Fury was asked whether his fight against Anthony Joshua had come too late for both boxers, the Gypsy King responded: “Is it too late?… It’s the icing on the cake of two great careers.”

Former heavyweight world champions Fury and ⁠⁠Joshua came face to face ⁠⁠in London on Wednesday to allay months-long fears and rumours surrounding their long-awaited fight, which has been confirmed for December 11 in Cardiff.

The British boxing stars are 38 and 36 years old, respectively, and have kept the boxing world waiting for years.

For many fans, why it took so long to agree on a fight is almost as big a question as who will win.

Neither boxer wanted to take the hit for delaying the biggest fight in British boxing history when they appeared in front of the media in London. Fury blamed Joshua, despite reports stating Joshua insisted the fight take place in the United Kingdom for the sake of home fans.

“You’ve been crying behind the scenes to get out of this fight,” Fury said. “I’ve checkmated you. You have to fight. I’ve said I’ll fight anywhere.”

But is the Gypsy King right? Can Fury vs Joshua live up to more than 10 years of hype?

Joshua and Fury are prizefighters who decide their destiny in the ring, but outside of it, their promoters negotiate contracts, choose venues and make calls on top billing.

The history goes back 10 years and is full of near misses, contractual problems and other fighters entering the fray.

It all started in 2020, when the two camps agreed to a two-fight deal. A year later, contracts were signed for an undisputed heavyweight showdown. However, Deontay Wilder, an American former world heavyweight champion, won an arbitration case that forced Fury into a trilogy fight in 2021.

In 2022, Joshua reportedly accepted a 60-40 purse split in Fury’s favour, but that deal collapsed too. During this period, unbeaten Ukrainian heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk defeated Joshua twice and proceeded to beat Fury twice as well.

All this while, Fury vs Joshua failed to materialise.

Online streaming platform Netflix, which holds global rights to the fight, has billed it as a collaboration between Saudi sports powerbroker Turki Alshikh’s The Ring magazine and Dana White, the owner of mixed martial arts promotion UFC.

Neither Joshua’s promoter, Eddie Hearn, nor Fury’s, Frank Warren, was named when talks of the fight resurfaced earlier this year.

Alshikh and White cofounded a boxing promotion, Zuffa Boxing, which was launched earlier this year and became a point of contention in the Joshua-Fury fight. Hearn was of the view that Joshua’s contract barred White and Zuffa’s parent company from any promotional role.

“Dana White cannot be involved with this fight promotion,” Hearn said recently.

However, Fury saw it differently and blamed Hearn for costing “the biggest fight in boxing history” in an Instagram post.

White was not seen at the London news conference, where fans booed his name.

In boxing, the name that comes first on the poster usually signals the A-side, or the bigger fighter.

Joshua claimed he got a call asking whether he minded Fury’s name going first, because Fury was “unwilling to sign unless he does”.

There was also the issue of the fight venue and, specifically, the host country.

Joshua insisted he ensured it would happen in the UK, whereas White had pushed for it to be held at Madison Square Garden in New York.

“I know we are going to inspire this generation, and I know for a fact we are going to inspire the next generation,” Joshua said.

The niceties didn’t last long between the opponents as Fury claimed he would knock Joshua out.

“I’m going to catch him and, when I do, it’s going to be curtains,” Fury said.

Joshua welcomed the outburst and said: “This is the energy that we want.”

In the end, money got the deal over the line.

Reports in UK media say the fighters will share a $200m purse and will bag more than “any British fighter has earned in a fight ever”.

articles.title: India vs Pakistan scheduled for October 10, 2027 at Cricket World Cup
articles.summary: The rivals have been grouped together again, along with holders Australia, as ICC announces schedule for the tournament.
articles.body:
Cricket’s most heated and biggest-selling fixture, India vs Pakistan, will have at least one meeting at the World Cup 2027, according to the schedule announced by the International Cricket Council (ICC).

Johannesburg will host the group-stage fixture between the bitter rivals, as well as the final, the ICC revealed in the schedule released on Thursday.

A total of 12 venues will host the matches between the 12 participants across three countries: South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe.

The India-Pakistan match is scheduled for October 10, 2027 in Johannesburg, which will also host the November 21, 2027 final.

The South Asian neighbours could meet for a second time in the Super Seven stage of the competition, and for a third time in the final, should both qualify for it.

It will be the fourth consecutive 50-over World Cup. The most lucrative group-stage match of the tournament will be guaranteed by drawing both India and Pakistan in the same group in a ballot held behind closed doors, unlike other major global sporting events.

The 12 nations are split into two groups:

Group A: Australia, India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe, qualifier. Group B: New Zealand, South Africa, Sri Lanka, England, Bangladesh, qualifier.

The two qualifiers will be confirmed after a 10-team tournament early next year. The winner will advance to the group stage of the mega event. The losing finalist and the two losing semifinalists will play the Super Series in Namibia ahead of the World Cup, with the winner advancing as the second qualifier.

The group stage of the tournament begins in Cape Town on October 7, 2027 when defending champions Australia take on India in a repeat of the 2023 World Cup final. Newlands in Cape Town, which has an iconic mountain backdrop, will also host a semifinal on November 17, 2027. The second semifinal on November 18 next year will be played at Centurion’s SuperSport Park.

The ICC said that the top 10 teams in its rankings as of Tuesday have gained automatic qualification. Zimbabwe, the cohosts of the tournament, begin their campaign on October 11, 2027 with a game against Afghanistan at Bulawayo.

“South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia will provide an unforgettable stage for the world’s best teams, combining a deep passion for cricket, extraordinary destinations and a renowned warmth of welcome,” ICC chairman Jay Shah said in a statement.

After the group stage, the top three teams from each group advance to the Super 7 stage. The seventh team will be the best fourth-place side across the two groups.

The ICC said that, to provide clarity for fans, teams and stakeholders, a number of teams have been pre-seeded into the designated Super 7 stage, no matter where they finish among the top three during the group stage.

England will play two group games in Namibia, while a newly built Victoria Falls ground in Zimbabwe hosts the final game of the group stage between the co-hosts and India on October 24, 2027. An additional three games in the Super 7 stage will also be hosted at the same venue.

The top four teams after the Super 7 phase advance to the semifinals. The top finisher will play against the fourth-placed team, with the second- and third-placed teams going head-to-head in the other semi-final.

articles.title: France vs Italy: UEFA Nations League – Zidane, Olise, Esposito, teams, form
articles.summary: France face neighbours Italy in new coach Zinedine Zidane’s first home game, with Mbappe out injured.
articles.body:
Who : France vs Italy What : UEFA Nations League 2026-27 , Group A1 match Where : Stade de France, Saint-Denis, France When : Friday, October 2, at 8:45pm local time (18:45 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 15:45 GMT.

It’s time for Zinedine Zidane’s homecoming.

Two-time world champions France face neighbours Italy in Friday’s Nations League match, with Zidane taking charge for the first time on home soil.

Appointed in late July as successor to Didier Deschamps , ex-captain Zidane has guided France to back-to-back away wins. Now he has the chance to complete a hat-trick of victories in front of Les Bleus faithful.

Despite losing captain Kylian Mbappe to injury , France have maintained their winning start, all thanks to their squad depth and talent across positions.

Like France, four-time World Cup winners Italy are also managed by a former player – Roberto Mancini – who is back in the job for the second time. Mancini’s first game back in charge ended in Roman jeers, but the Azzurri responded in style with an emphatic win in their second game.

Friday’s match is expected to be played in front of what will be a sell-out crowd of close to 80,000 fans at the national stadium north of Paris.

So, can Italy build on their dazzling display or will France give Zidane more reasons to rejoice?

Al Jazeera breaks down everything in this match preview:

The UEFA Nations League was founded in 2018 to reduce the number of meaningless friendlies and give nations competitive matches against top-ranked teams.

In this competition, countries from across Europe participate in a league structure which features promotion and relegation.

How have France and Italy played in the Nations League?

France are on top of this group with six points after identical 1-0 wins over Turkiye and Belgium .

Italy, on the other hand, are second-to-last with three points after losing 2-0 to Belgium and thrashing Turkiye 4-1.

They last met in a Nations League group match in November 2024.

France defeated Italy 3-1 in Milan then, with a double from Adrien Rabiot and a Guglielmo Vicario own goal. Andrea Cambiaso netted the consolation goal for the Italians.

Michael Olise and Desire Doue (France): Olise’s outrageous finish in Monday’s Belgium game had Zidane going berserk on the sideline. Such is his talent. He has been involved in both goals France scored in this year’s Nations League and is also enjoying a flying start at Bayern Munich this term with eight goals and four assists. Doue, 21, is equally impressive – he assisted Olise in the last game, earning player of the match.

Francesco Pio Esposito and Davide Frattesi (Italy): Pio Esposito not only scored a goal in the last game but also celebrated a sweet bit of history – he and his older brother Sebastiano played against Turkiye, marking the first time two brothers started for Italy in more than a century. Inter Milan striker Pio already has five goals in 10 Azzurri appearances. Italian fans should also watch out for Frattesi, another scorer from the last game who has also netted three times for Lazio in this year’s Serie A.

Zinedine Zidane (France): “It is going to be really emotional,” said Zidane, whose last appearance at the Stade de France came as a player in a friendly against Mexico in 2006.

Roberto Mancini (Italy): “Facing Zidane will be a pleasure, but this isn’t a duel between us,” assured Mancini in his press conference.

“It is going to be a great game between France and Italy, teams who are still trying to figure things out. Whatever happens, I feel that this match will be very useful for the process.”

Mbappe is the biggest name missing from the France squad. He picked up a knee injury after scoring the winning goal against Turkiye and has since been sidelined for two weeks.

Elsewhere, central midfielder Warren Zaire-Emery is out with a thigh injury, and Matteo Guendouzi remains suspended.

articles.title: Shenzhen Open: Judd Trump beats Si Jiahui to set up Mark Selby tie
articles.summary: Judd Trump defeats Si Jiahui 5-2 to set up a mouthwatering quarter-final meeting with Mark Selby at the Shenzhen Open.
articles.body:
Judd Trump defeated Si Jiahui 5-2 to set up a mouthwatering quarter-final meeting with Mark Selby at the Shenzhen Open.

The Englishman reeled off breaks of 80, 71, 53 and 54, though his route to victory over China's Si was almost derailed by a bizarre glitch with the LED advertising screen behind the table.

Having watched Si miss the yellow in the seventh frame, world number two Trump showed his frustration as the screen flashed blue in his line of sight as he potted the same ball into the top-right pocket.

However, he was able to regain his composure and clear the remaining colours to seal the win.

"At this stage there's always a crucial ball or crucial frame," said Trump.

"So far this season and maybe last season I have not been winning those. But that can change at any point - you have just got to keep putting yourself in those positions."

Four-time world champion Selby, who won the China Open in August, compiled a top break of 99 in his 5-3 triumph over Stephen Maguire.

In the other last-16 matches, world champion Wu Yize beat Ricky Walden by the same score and will next face Shaun Murphy in a repeat of their Crucible final in May.

Murphy dominated his encounter with Elliot Slessor to record a 5-1 win, while Yuan Sijun swept Zak Surety aside 5-2 and Jimmy Robertson thrashed Scott Donaldson 5-0.

Neil Robertson fell to a 5-2 loss to Chris Wakelin and Kyren Wilson also exited with a 5-2 defeat by Michael Holt, who knocked in a superb break of 126 on his way to reaching his first quarter-final in a ranking event since the UK Championship in 2024.

articles.title: World Grand Prix: James Wade still feels the nerves despite competing at the unique event for the 22nd time in his career
articles.summary: James Wade speaks openly on the "hellish" World Grand Prix double-start format and why he believes Gary Anderson is the "best scorer" he has ever seen;you can watch World Grand Prix Darts live on Sky Sports until Sunday
articles.body:
The 43-year-old, who last lifted a major trophy at the UK Open in 2021, continued his bid for a third World Grand Prix after producing a superb display to defeat Stephen Bunting 3-1 in the unique double-start format in Leicester.

Wade averaged 93.20 and fired in 15 140s, defying a 96 average from Bunting to book his place in the last eight.

"I just felt like it was timing at the right place and the right time. It wasn't the right place for Stephen," Wade, nicknamed 'The Machine ', told Sky Sports' Polly James.

"I was better than average, I think. I am just grateful to win. It's so hard to win a double start.

"We can all play it cool and pretend to be relaxed and enjoying the game. But it's awful, it's hellish.

"It's not very nice. It's graft and just really hard work. We're not all cool, we are working very hard."

Wade, who took in a local art gallery in Leicester as part of his preparations, was asked whether he is currently playing some of the best darts of his career.

"Nowhere near really," he replied. "But I am having to play better against better players. I've got loads more gears to go.

"But talk is cheap and I am full of cheap talk."

Speaking at his press conference, Wade said: "I get nervous, I make myself feel ill, I don't want to get involved in it.

"I just want it to be over and done with quick.

"So am I well equipped or do I just deal with the c***** end of the stick better than others? It's so nerve-wracking; it's awful."

Wade also hailed Gary Anderson as one of the greatest ever, despite 'The Flying Scotsman' exiting the tournament following a landmark 3-1 win for Dutchman Niels Zonneveld .

On Anderson's legacy in the sport, Wade said: "I've played against every dart player in the world and he is the best scorer in the world when he's at his very best.

"I think those days are gone now. I don't think we're going to see that scoring from Gary Anderson ever again, but when he was on he was the best scorer I've ever seen.

"I'm not put on a pedestal like that and it is what it is. I'm just happy to still be about and still whooping the youngsters, so that's good."

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade storm into quarter-finals as Gary Anderson eliminated
articles.summary: Luke Humphries goes at 74 per cent on his starting doubles and 64 per cent on his closing ones as he sweeps Jermaine Wattimena 3-0, will face Niels Zonneveld in last eight after Dutch debutant dispatches Gary Anderson; James Wade excels against Stephen Bunting
articles.body:
There were also 3-1 victories for James Wade and Niels Zonneveld over Stephen Bunting and Gary Anderson respectively, while Gian Van Veen came through a deciding-set cracker with Ryan Searle to triumph 3-2.

Humphries - the title favourite after defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night - had averaged only 80 and gone at 26 per cent on his closing doubles in a scruffy 2-0 win over Dave Chisnall on Tuesday evening.

Two nights later, the 2023 champion and 2024 and 2025 runner-up averaged 94.11 and secured a finishing-double percentage of 64, although his starting-double percentage of 74 was the most eye-catching stat as he peppered double 16 early in legs.

'Cool Hand' - who will face Wattimena's fellow Dutchman Zonneveld in the last eight on Friday - hit his 10-darter at the start of the third set, while Wattimena twice hit the wrong double in the opening set.

Humphries said afterwards: "I've got a good chance of winning this. At the moment I'm a bit up and down, but if I can put that right I'm going to be tough to beat.

"It wasn't the best performance, but it was a good performance. It was a lot better than it was on Tuesday.

"I think I got in every time with my first three darts. When you're doing stuff like that, it's going to take a top performance to beat you."

Wade, meanwhile, delivered a starting masterclass to reach his eighth World Grand Prix quarter-final, hitting an opening shot of 160 five times during his win over Bunting.

The sixth seed dropped his standards in the third set but was electric in the other three as he set up a meeting with Van Veen.

Wade said: "I am so grateful as it is so hard to win with a double start. We can all play it cool and pretend to be relaxed but it is awful, it is hellish, really hard work.

"I don't feel anywhere near my best but I am having to play better against better players. I have loads more gears to go - but talk is cheap.

Van Veen wins thriller to secure Wade showdown

Elsewhere, Searle - who landed a 167 checkout, the highest of the week - threw for the match against Van Veen after breaking the Dutchman with a finish of 100 in the fourth set, only to be broken straightaway in the deciding leg.

Van Veen, who had led 2-0 in the penultimate set before being pegged back to 2-2 by Searle, then blitzed the final set 3-0.

The third seed said: "When I was 2-1 down in sets, I was like, 'oh no, this is not how I want to go out'.

"As good as double 16 went for me in the first round, it kind of bothered me today. But at the end it really came good.

"I was quite happy with my scoring, but just missed a couple of darts at a crucial time. Luckily I got the job done."

Anderson tumbles out as Zonneveld's run continues

Van Veen's compatriot Zonneveld followed his opening-round win over Josh Rock by dumping out Anderson, starting by winning a first set in which every leg went against the throw.

Anderson made a terrible start to the match, hitting single one and then suffering two bounce-outs, while he was the victim of another bounce-out in the fourth set as he aimed for a leg-winning bullseye.

Zonneveld subsequently broke before closing out victory in the next leg.

The 28-year-old said: "Especially in this tournament, it is one of the biggest things in my whole career.

"I have achieved many things Pro Tour-wise and Euro Tour-wise but not on the main stage, just once at the World Series Finals.

"I have become a dad so less sleep and all that but I feel in rhythm again."

articles.title: Gary Bettman Expresses Concern About Use of No-Trade Clauses Amid Rise in NHL Trade Requests
articles.summary: NHL commissioner Gary Bettman isn't pleased with how players are using no-trade or no-movement clauses in order to facilitate deals to other teams.
articles.body:
NHL commissioner Gary Bettman isn't pleased with how players are using no-trade or no-movement clauses in order to facilitate deals to other teams.

"As I look at what's happened or is happening now, I don't think that's a good thing," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said Thursday on Sportsnet 590's FAN Hockey Show with Matt Marchese and Michael Futa. "I don't think it's good for the player, I don't think it's good for the club, I don't think it's good for fans watching and their connection to the game."

6 Players on Trade Watch After Marchenko-Knies Deal

B/R NHL Trade Block Big Board for October 2026

ESPN's Greg Wyshynski provided four examples of players using their clauses in their favor.

Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk used a NMC to head to the Florida Panthers and play on the same team as his brother, Matthew Tkachuk.

Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Zach Werenski blocked a trade to the Dallas Stars after he reportedly told his team he had no plans to re-sign with them in 2028, when his contract runs out.

Detroit Red Wings center and captain Dylan Larkin covets a trade but initially had a list of just three locations where he was willing to go, per Helene St. James of the Detroit Free Press (Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights or Florida Panthers). The team list now includes the Colorado Avalanche, Washington Capitals, Dallas Stars and Tampa Bay Lightning, per Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman .

In addition, Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck has issued a trade request and has not reported to the team this year.

Bettman isn't thrilled with what he's seen and provided more commentary on the matter, per Sportsnet.

"This notion now where, a) you can select where you want to go to and b) you can demand a trade. ... That was never the original intention," Bettman said. "If this becomes a problem — I don't think one off-season a problem makes — but if this becomes a problem, it's something we're going to have to discuss with the players' association.

"While it may be good for a player in a particular case, though based on what we're seeing now, I'm not so sure it's good for the player either, but we have to look at what's good for the game, good for the players overall, good for the league, and so it's something we're going to keep an eye on."

As Wyshynski noted, NHL agent Allan Walsh provided pushback on Bettman's claims.

The current collective bargaining agreement runs through the 2029-30 season. In theory, the league could bring this up to the NHLPA in negotiations a few years down the road.

In the meantime, some of the futures of the game's biggest stars remain in a holding pattern as the season begins. We'll see what happens soon enough.

articles.title: Nets' Josh Minott speaks on new role after veteran additions
articles.summary: Brooklyn Nets forward Josh Minott could be looking at a new role this season after Brooklyn's free-agent additions and he explains his mindset.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Brooklyn Nets forward Josh Minott is heading into his second season with the Nets after spending time with winning teams in the Minnesota Timberwolves and Boston Celtics. Brooklyn traded for Minott in the middle of last season and it didn't take long for him to show why teams covet him. Minott could be headed for a different role this season, but he's understanding of that.

"I'd say everything starts defensively. If you don't have that, you really don't have anything. For my last two teams, you couldn't even think about or dream of touching the court without defense," Minott said during his Media Day interview on Monday. Minott came off the bench for head coach Jordi Fernandez last season, but his defense and athleticism allowed him to have some signature moments on the floor.

"I understand we have some some new pieces now, some ball-dominant pieces. I've seen the work Julius can do in the post and his creation out of there. So, I'd say just focusing on finding spots, playing off-ball," Minott continued. "I understand I probably won't be running any offense, which I got no problem with, but just more finding ways to impact the game."

Minott, 23 , is coming off a 2025-26 NBA season in which he averaged 7.4 points and 3.2 rebounds per game while shooting 50.0% from the field and 41.8% from behind the three-point line. In his 16 games with the Nets after being acquired from the Celtics, Minott averaged 10.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per game while shooting 49.1% from the floor and 39.5% from deep.

With Brooklyn adding forward Julius Randle to a lineup that already has forward Michael Porter Jr. and guard Egor Demin, Minott is likely looking at a bench role for this season. Minott, who re-signed with the Nets this offseason on a two-year, $9 million contract, does not know what his role will be, but he is ready to provide whatever he can to make an impact on one of the youngest teams in the league.

articles.title: LSU football player under investigation for alleged rape
articles.summary: LSU defensive end Damien Shanklin is being investigated by the East Baton Rouge District Attorney's Office and LSU police after being accused of rape.
articles.body:
Louisiana authorities are investigating an LSU football player for alleged rape of a female student.

A police report was filed by a woman who said defensive end Damien Shanklin raped her in October 2025. A Title IX case on matter initially resulted in Shanklin being found responsible for "forcible rape" and suspended one year, but an appeal reduced the suspension to probation, according to ESPN .

Now, the East Baton Rouge District Attorney's Office is investigating the matter after the woman made her allegations public in a TikTok video Sept. 14. LSU police are also investigating, ESPN reports.

USA TODAY's policy is not to identify victims of alleged sexual assault unless they agree to be named.

Grant L. Willis and Morgan H. Johnson, attorneys for Shanklin from the Taylor Porter Law firm, said in a statement to USA TODAY Sports the LSU player maintains his innocence and will fully cooperate in the investigation.

"What has been portrayed on social media and in the news thus far, is not a full account of all of the facts and circumstances surrounding this situation," the statement read. "Given this is an ongoing criminal investigation, all facts are not publicly available to not compromise the criminal investigation. We simply ask that the court of public opinion cease to make any assumptions about any person involved until more information is publicly available."

Shanklin's attorney's added he will not have any further comment until the investigation is complete.

Citing Title IX documents, ESPN reported Shanklin and the woman agreed their initial contact inside Shanklin's residence hall room was consensual, but he had penetrative sex with her without her consent for nearly 20 seconds before she told him to stop. She went to a nearby hospital to get a rape kit and alleges he sent her $1,000 so she wouldn't press charges, and that Shanklin's mother contacted her to ask her the same.

LSU confirmed the incident was reported by the woman and Shanklin a few days afterward but no criminal complaint was filed at the time. The Title IX investigation found Shanklin responsible for "forcible rape," which resulted in a one-year suspension from all campus activities. Shanklin appealed it and in August, Administrative Law Judge Janet Waguespack reduced the punishment to a probation that allowed Shanklin to remain enrolled and able to participate in activities.

After the Title IX investigation was appealed by Shanklin and resulted in a lesser sentence, the woman went public.

"That made my anxiety really, really bad because I don't want to face this person, so this caused me to go online full time, and now I'm just trying to speak on my story because LSU does really protect their athletes, especially their football players," the woman said in her TikTok video. "I really just wanted to bring awareness upon this situation because I'm just dealing with a lot right now, and I think that this story needs to be heard."

LSU stated it "properly followed" its Title IX policy and processes to reach a conclusion.

"LSU and its current administration take very seriously any allegations of misconduct involving students on our campuses. Safety and security must be our number one priority," said university president Wade Rousse. "Let me assure everyone that this incident has been handled professionally and that LSU has strictly followed our policies, procedures and best practices, including the Title IX process, to guide our actions to date.

"Now that a criminal complaint has been filed, our role is to continue cooperating with our law enforcement partners as they work through their investigatory process."

Shanklin is a second-year player for the Tigers after making five appearances in his freshman season in 2025. He has not seen any action during the 2026 season, and he was not practicing with the team prior to the start of the campaign.

"He is not practicing with the team right now and that's all I can comment on that," first-year coach Lane Kiffin said about Shanklin's status on Aug. 12.

LSU football did not immediately respond to a request asking if Shanklin remains on the team.

The Netherlands recovered from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Greece in Thessaloniki, extending their unbeaten run in competitive matches to 19 games.

Greece started strongly and thought they had taken the lead through Christos Tzolis , but his effort was ruled out for offside before an injury forced the forward off.

The hosts eventually broke through in the 23rd minute. Fotis Ioannidis collected Georgios Masouras ' flick-on before advancing into the area and calmly finding the bottom corner.

Greece doubled their advantage just before the interval when Ioannidis turned provider, sending Masouras through to finish.

The Netherlands emerged with greater purpose after the break and reduced the deficit shortly before the hour mark. Virgil Van Dijk rose highest to head home from Joey Veerman 's corner.

The visitors continued to dominate and finally found their equaliser in the 89th minute. Tijjani Reijnders met Noa Lang 's delivery with a powerful volley to rescue a point.

The result leaves Greece top of Group A2, with the Netherlands also unbeaten.
